155	### Core Rules
156	
157	*Conventions.* Rules are named `IW-n` (In-World); each states a **Rule** (what the player sees and the contract with neighbours), a **Why** and **Edge notes**. Formulas are `D.n` (Formulas section: D.1 needle angle, D.2 zone intervals, D.3 honest numeral, D.4 settle, D.5 tremor, D.6 card layout, D.7 legibility table, D.8 instrument budget, D.9 gleam edge, D.10 reduced-motion substitutes, D.11 linear instruments, D.12 `lsb` visibility lint). Conflicts are `K-n` (K-1..K-14 from the brief, K-15 and K-16 raised by the ux-designer, K-17 and K-18 raised in this stage); open questions `OQ-IW-n`. "(advisor ruling Rn)", "(checkpoint ruling Cn)" and "(Xn)" are provenance labels from the authoring run: the `rulings.md` they cite is not on disk and **no rulings digest exists in this document**; the rule each label governs is stated in the clause or rule that cites it, and a label is never the only statement of a rule *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the earlier claim that a digest at the end of Open Questions restates every ruling was false and is withdrawn); "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" marks a place where two specialists disagreed and this GDD picked one. Values that are this GDD's own and not yet registered are `[PLACEHOLDER]`; values quoted from a neighbour carry their owner and are never changed here. Implementation choices are tagged "-> ADR candidate" and kept out of the rules. **Chest-lamp sweep:** the beam origin is the per-facing chest point (PC); the lamp is hands-free; thrown Chemlight glowsticks (`#86B896`) light a gauge exactly as the beam does; no "hand lamp" wording appears anywhere in this document.
158	
159	**Rule index.** Group A, what this system is: IW-1 ownership, IW-2 presentation-only, IW-3 lit-only readability, IW-4 housing pip, IW-5 reading source. Group B, the instrument family: IW-6 taxonomy, IW-7 dial template, IW-8 data and calibration record, IW-9 quantity set, IW-10 the needle element. Group C, honest motion: IW-11 continuous change and settle, IW-12 tremor, IW-13 motion-mode dispatch, IW-14 readouts, IW-15 zone bands. Group D, lying surfaces and state frames: IW-16 the gleam, IW-17 Module-Body Presenter, IW-18 WORN, IW-19 alarm mark, IW-20 sight-glass and linear instruments. Group E, the inspect view: IW-21 targeting, IW-22 card content, IW-23 placement, IW-24 lifecycle, IW-25 input and falsification, IW-26 parity. Group F, boundaries: IW-27 reduced motion, IW-28 never-do list, IW-29 manifest floors, IW-30 DEAD binding, IW-31 placement record, IW-32 sound, IW-33 pause and restore, IW-34 fallbacks, IW-35 flagged not edited, IW-36 legibility contract, IW-37 strings, IW-38 diagnostics.
160	
161	#### Group A. What this system is
162	
163	**IW-1. Ownership: module-body reading surfaces.**
164	*Rule.* In-World Instruments owns (a) every gauge, dial, level sight-glass and state glyph produced by the ship or a derelict, drawn as lit sprites on layer 0; (b) the inspect card on layer 2, the same instrument at HUD size; (c) the **Module-Body Presenter**: the selection among a module sheet's *honest* state frames and the drawing of the state glyph (IW-17). It owns no module art (Item DB `sprite_family` names the sheet and state tokens), no placement (Layout and Derelict Authoring), no behaviour of the module, and no decision about whether, when, for whom or by how much anything lies (Filter and Sanity). It never calls `true_value`. Every reading produced by the ship or a derelict is this GDD's; Suit & Equipment and HUD & Suit Layer own only suit-produced and hand-tool readings (advisor ruling R7, R24).
165	*Why.* IDX:39 and ART 7.0 ("the ship is an instrument": who produced the number decides where it is drawn). No sibling claims the presenter (DA:1340, FT:232, IA:920, PF:1461). DA:1571's row assigning "gauges and instruments reading authored systems" to "the suit and HUD" is a stale assignment, refreshed by its owner (K-4).
166	*Edge notes.* The index has no row naming the module presenter (K-11): flagged to the producer, not edited here (IW-35).
167	
168	**IW-2. Presentation-only, zero registrations.**
169	*Rule.* Instruments are `PRESENTATION` subscribers (KRN:106-110; PIPE PR-8). They read `SIM` and `PERCEPTION_OUT` views and write only CanvasItem, Material, Light2D, particle and audio-request state; never a block, a command, a hook or a mutator. A notification is a dirty mark; reading and drawing happen in the render callback; placement is integer base px; nothing here can cause a tick. The card is **not** an `INPUT_SURFACE`: it issues no commands. The Controller's Adapter (an `INPUT_SURFACE`) owns the `inspect_card` context and publishes a presentation-local signal `{context, inspect_ref}` (registry: `inspect_card_context_signal`) that Instruments subscribe to (IW-25). Instruments register no block, hook, mutator, dirty key or persisted field (advisor ruling R22; K-1).
170	*Why.* PR-8 rule 1 (PIPE:188): `INPUT_SURFACE` only "if it also issues commands — the HUD's prompts do not; the chart table does" (PIPE's example only: per Chart Table CT-27, the chart table holds the `INPUT_SURFACE` class for VS-B and submits nothing at MVP). Instruments submit nothing.
171	*Edge notes.* Refresh owed by the Controller: PC-16 (PC:147: "an `INPUT_SURFACE` of In-World Instruments"), PC:77's purpose column ("Interaction's inspect verb", contradicting IA-38), PC:210 row 10 (K-1, K-12).
172	
173	**IW-3. Lit-only readability: "What You Light, You Can Read".**
174	*Rule.* A world gauge is readable exactly as far as the world lighting makes its pixels visible: Instruments do **not** gate the drawing of a world gauge on `lit(ref)`; the lit renderer and the HullSurface material make an unlit face dark. Two things are gated on the Emitter State bit `lit(ref)` (hysteresis `LIT_ON_PM` 150 / `LIT_OFF_PM` 120, no dwell; owner technical-artist; EM-22): the **inspect prompt** (Interaction's, IW-21) and the **inspect card** (IW-24). No instrument is an emitter and no gauge is a lantern. Mechanical gauges need no power to be read at MVP, so a dead loop's gauge shows its reading as soon as light reaches it. Thrown Chemlight glowsticks and fixtures light a gauge as the beam does.
175	*Why.* P3: reading spends light. Gating the card by the sim bit and the face by the renderer keeps one source of light truth each (ART 7.0 "unreadable until lit"; LO:436; EM:864).
176	*Edge notes.* Between `LIT_OFF_PM` and `LIT_ON_PM` the face may be dimly visible while the card is refused: intended (precision costs more light than a glance). Gauge motion is updated whether or not the face is lit (cheap, and a face entering the beam shows its current needle on its first lit frame); the gleam is "lit with its host" and needs no lit query (PF-16). The face is never shown or hidden by `lit(ref)` in code, so the 150/120 hysteresis cannot make a face flash at a pool edge (HR-13); only the prompt and the card are lit-gated, and the card needs a fresh press to reopen. Whether a gauge needs power at a later tier is OQ-IW-11.
177	
178	**IW-4. Self-emission is a non-readable housing pip, and the pip is corruptible.**
179	*Rule.* "A running loop's gauge is faintly lit by its own emission" (ART 7.0) is realised as a small loop-hue **housing pip** (size `[PLACEHOLDER]`, 4x2 art px proposed by the art-director, 2x2 by the ux-designer; OQ-IW-12) on the emissive layer (mask bit 2, casts no light, exposes nothing; LO-14, LO:225). It exists only while the bound subject's `served_pm` > 0, lets the player *find* a running gauge in the dark, and does **not** make the face readable and does **not** make `lit(ref)` true. It is drawn through the `HOUSING_GLOW(ref)` ref, so it is stage-2 corruptible: finding a gauge by its pip is not proof its loop runs. Its emission is capped at or below fixture glow and well below the beam (`PIP_EMIT_MAX`, set by the Lighting spike, ART 8.12); the hull/integrity loop has no pip (it has no running medium) (advisor ruling R21; K-6).
180	*Why.* Keeps `lit(ref)`, the card, Sanity's lit-entry and P3 consistent without adding emitters or an Emitter State change (LO-14's channel rule: "a lamp housing's own emissive sprite ... read the Filter channel and may lie").
181	*Edge notes.* The pip carries **presence or absence only** ("something here is running"); loop identity is the housing's fitting silhouette (IW-7), so the hue-removed test is met by silhouette and by the pip's on/off state. The fixture lamp's brightness from `served_pm` is consequence channel and is never confused with the pip, which casts no pool.
182	
183	**IW-5. Reading source: one pull per instrument per frame; never cache; never read truth.**
184	*Rule.* In the render callback each on-screen instrument in a loaded section obtains its displayed value with exactly one `perceived(ref, viewer)` call (PF-7), `viewer` being the local seat's `PlayerId`; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* one **`InstrumentPresenter` per instrument** is the sole caller of `perceived()` for its ref and the sole owner of the settle, tremor, dwell and notch scalars, and the wall node and the card are views of the frame index and digits it publishes once per frame (the Filter's `(ref, viewer, frame)` memo is the backstop; ADR candidate, X-6). An instrument never stores a `Perceived` record across frames, never addresses the Filter by `peer_id` (PF-10), and never calls `true_value`, `summary()` (a ship-status read), `power_use()` (Attention's stimulus) or `can_join()`. It may read `read_view` only for **non-value** inputs: the tremor predicate (IW-12), module frame selection and WORN (IW-17, IW-18), the alarm predicate (IW-19), and binding validity (IW-30). Those reads are refreshed once per Graph step (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6), not per frame, and never feed a displayed value. The needle target is `displayed_pm`. The honest tremor offset is multiplied by `tremor_weight_pm / 1000` from the same pull (IW-12, D.5). The presentation-local scalars now also include `env_hold` (the tremor envelope latched at the first non-HONEST frame; discarded at `tremor_weight_pm` 0, `hard_start`, cull, cut and restore), which is drawing state like the settle triple, never a cached `Perceived`. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* An instrument that is off-screen or in an unloaded section pulls nothing; on its first pull after being culled it **snaps** to `displayed_pm` with no settle and no interpolation from stale history (history older than one Graph step is meaningless, and a settle on re-entry would be a motion with no world cause, P1) (advisor ruling R18).
185	*Why.* PF-8: the record never contains the truth while a lie is active; caching would let a stale record outlive a lie's end. R18 and PF-3: only the Filter wraps a true value.
186	*Edge notes.* Presentation-local scalars (the settle triple, `prev_honest_pm` and the rest, window and reversal-dwell scalars of IW-11, tremor onset and decay timestamps, `env_hold`, the numeral throttle timestamp) are derived drawing state, not cached `Perceived` records: each is a pure function of values the player was already shown, none is read by another system, all are discarded on restore, cull and camera cut. **CONFLICT K-17 (new): LSG:998 and LS-20 (LSG:201) (locked) say "gauges read `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles" (LS-20: "Instruments and Audio poll `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles")**, which contradicts R18/PF-3 (a gauge never reads a value from `read_view`). This GDD follows R18 and PF-3: value reads go only through `perceived`; the "smooth needles" of LSG:998 and LS-20 is delivered by IW-11's interpolation, not by a value read. The Graph's own sentences are routed to its owner as a refresh. Related: the honest path carries no previous value, which IW-11 answers with the local scalar `prev_honest_pm` (K-17, checkpoint ruling C14).
187	
188	#### Group B. The instrument family
189	
190	**IW-6. Taxonomy: wall instrument kinds and the card's numeral; one definition at two scales.**
191	*Rule.* Every instrument is one data definition (`assets/data/instruments/<instrument_id>`, IW-8) rendered by one scene definition at two scales: the wall or panel node (layer 0, art px x `k`) and the card (layer 2, HUD art px x `H`). The kinds:
192	
193	| Kind | `gauge_kind` | World form (no numerals, ART 3.1) | Card form | Motion signatures | Lie reach (SN-16) | Sizes |
194	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
195	| Dial | DIAL | open 240-degree arc strip on a chamfered rectangular housing; separate pivoted needle; zone bands; hub | same dial at HUD px, label, numeral | settle, tremor, glide (with wander) | needle: stage 1 | DIAL_L, DIAL_S (IW-7) |
196	| Level sight-glass | LINEAR | vertical glass tube, fluid column, meniscus bead, side zone strip and ticks | same glass, label, numeral | settle, tremor, glide (linear branch, D.11) | meniscus: stage 1 | one size at MVP, `travel_px` 50 `[PLACEHOLDER]` (IW-20) |
197	| Numeral | READOUT | **none in the world** | digit cells in a glass-edged well | honest step per real change; lie: continuous tick or stale hold (PF-18) | numeral: stage 1 | card only |
198	| State glyph | GLYPH | 8x8 lens mark on a module housing; two shape-coded frames (run, stop); no flow mark, no loop hue | not carried | frame swap (no needle motion) | stage 2 | 8x8 |
199	| Machine frame | FRAME | the module's own state frames (IW-17) | not carried | frame cut, rotor cadence | stage 3 (SPRITE_SWAP) | module cell (96x96) |
200	
201	Housing glow frames (the lamp lit/unlit pair) and the pip (IW-4) ride the `HOUSING_GLOW` ref (stage 2). The stage-1 "readout" of SN-16 is the card's numeral, which is `displayed_value` of the `.needle` ref's `Perceived` (the digit tick of PF-18 acts there; TICK and STALE govern the numeral only, IW-13); it is not a second lie surface. A wall gauge carries no digit. The SN-16 "readout" wording is routed to Sanity and the `motion_mode` field description and PF-18 to the Filter as a wording refresh (checkpoint ruling C2).
202	*(orchestrator ruling: the ux-designer proposed an 8-pip drum ladder as an in-world "digital readout"; the art-director and ui-programmer proposed card-only. Card-only is adopted: a pip ladder is a numeral in disguise against ART 3.1, doubles the asset set for a solo developer and adds a lie surface with no witness value beyond the needle. The battery-stock instruments become DIAL_S `stock` dials in the manifest, IW-29.)*
203	*Why.* One calibration for the Filter (PF-45), one test set, one art load; the card is "the same instrument magnified" by construction.
204	*Edge notes.* A decorative gauge that carries no remote, magnitude or trend information beyond its local witness is forbidden (IW-29). The loop identity of an instrument is never carried by dial geometry (IW-7).
205	
206	**IW-7. Dial template family: two authored sizes, one arc.**
207	*Rule.* All dials use `arc_deg` 240 (open sector at the bottom; the arc runs -120 to +120 degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock). Two authored sizes (registry: `dial_size_class`): **DIAL_L** `needle_len_px` 24 in a 96x48 prop cell and **DIAL_S** `needle_len_px` 18 in a 48x48 cell. Both are at or above `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` 16 (owner: this GDD; value unchanged, range 14.3-32) and glide-eligible: `rate_floor` = max(0.5, 28.6 / `needle_len_px`) = 1.19 deg/s at 24 and 1.59 deg/s at 18, inside the 0.5-2.0 band (PF-13, PF-17). Loop identity is the housing's fitting silhouette (ART 3.4, 7.2 table) plus the running-only pip, never dial geometry or face hue. Geometry (art px; pivot at the arc centre; band inner radius = needle length + 1; one geometry set, fixed by checkpoint ruling C5; the pixel mock S-A1 confirms the DIAL_S bezel only):
208	
209	| Size | Needle | Band inner r | Band thickness | Outer r | Arc width (2 x outer r) | Arc height (1.5 x outer r) | Housing (DIAL_L bezel 2 px, DIAL_S bezel 1 px, each side) | Cell | Cell margin |
210	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
211	| DIAL_L | 24 | 25 | 3 | 28 | 56 | 42 | 60 x 46 | 96x48 | 36 px horizontal, 2 px vertical |
212	| DIAL_S | 18 | 19 | 3 | 22 | 44 | 33 | 46 x 35 (bezel 1 px each side) | 48x48 | 1 px each side horizontally, 13 px vertically in total |
213	
214	*Arithmetic.* A 240-degree arc centred on 12 o'clock reaches its full width at the 3 and 9 o'clock points (|x| = r) and its lowest point at the end stops (y = r cos 120 = -0.5 r), so height = r (above the pivot) + 0.5 r (below) = 1.5 r. Needle stroke is 2 art px (HR-12: a stroke is at least 2 screen px at every `k`). The outer radius is the band's inner radius plus its thickness: DIAL_L 25 + 3 = 28 (arc 2 x 28 = 56 wide, 1.5 x 28 = 42 high, housing 56 + 4 = 60 by 42 + 4 = 46 with a 2 px bezel), DIAL_S 19 + 3 = 22 (arc 2 x 22 = 44 wide, 1.5 x 22 = 33 high, housing 44 + 2 = 46 by 33 + 2 = 35 with a 1 px bezel). The DIAL_S band is **3 rows** because IW-15 needs three patterns (solid, hatched, notched) that can be told apart; a 2-row band could not carry them. In the 48x48 cell the DIAL_S housing leaves 48 - 46 = 2 px horizontally (1 px each side) and 48 - 35 = 13 px vertically in total; DIAL_L leaves 96 - 60 = 36 px horizontally and 48 - 46 = 2 px vertically. The 1-px DIAL_S bezel is a minimum-feature exception routed to the art-director under BR-9 (ART 5.6); S-A1 confirms the bezel only, the radii are fixed. **Helmet-scale test (ART:714; the crewmate helmet is a 16 px circle; a round feature must be < 5.3 or > 32 art px):** sweep diameter 2L = 48 (DIAL_L) and 36 (DIAL_S), outer arc diameter 56 (DIAL_L) and **44** (DIAL_S, > 32), hub 4 (< 5.3): all pass. A dial at exactly `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` 16 has a 32 px sweep, on the boundary, so 16 is the Filter's eligibility floor and **not an authored size** (advisor ruling R25). The dial is never a closed circle; the 3.1 silhouette test is run on both housings (AC-IW-9). **Mounting (orchestrator ruling: art-director's terminal-fitting rule adopted over the ux-designer's housing-over-fitting-cell proposal).** Neither dial fits inside the pipe band (rows 29-58 of the 72 px face; ART 6.3 rule 7): DIAL_L (46 high) is a cap-less wall-hung panel or machine-panel instrument and is never mounted on a pipe run; DIAL_S (35 high) attaches at a pipe's **terminal fitting** (pipes never dead-end without one, ART 6.3 rule 1), centred on the band's mid-row (43.5, spanning about rows 26-61), so "pipe -> gauge" reads as a sentence; the exception to ART 6.3 rule 7 ("except an instrument seated on a terminal fitting") is a bible refresh owed by the art-director (BR-2). A MACHINE_PANEL dial of either size sits inside the module's 96x96 node. Wall gauges take the host face's sort origin (PIPE:129, :137). (advisor ruling R6, R25; K-7)
215	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Lower-sector arithmetic (the fitting plate).** The open sector below the pivot is bounded by the rays 60 degrees either side of straight down, so at depth `y` below the pivot its half-width is `y x tan 60` = 1.732 `y`; its floor is the arc's lowest points, at `y` = 0.5 x outer r (14 on DIAL_L, 11 on DIAL_S), and the housing's outer bottom edge is that plus the bezel (16 and 12). A plate of half-width `w` needs its top row at `y` >= `w` / 1.732. DIAL_L: the 16-px plate (`w` 8) starts at row 5 (4.62 rounded up), and the earlier 12-px height would end at row 17, 2.62 px past the arc floor and 1 px past the outer edge; the plate is therefore **16x11**, seated on the bottom bezel and ending exactly on the outer edge at row 16. DIAL_S: the 12-px plate (`w` 6) starts at row 4 (3.46 rounded up) and the 8-px height ends at row 12, exactly the outer edge (1-px bezel), so **12x8 stands**, also seated on the bezel. Both plates overlay the bottom bezel and overflow nothing; S-A1 confirms the silhouettes at 16x11 and 12x8. The LINEAR bead is **6 wide x 2 tall** (the width of the 6-px tube); the earlier "2x6" read as 2 wide x 6 tall, which fits neither the tube nor the 4-px caps. With a 54-px interior and `travel_px` 50 the bead spans rows 0-1 at empty and 50-51 at full, clear of both caps. Plate and bead extents are in the S-A1 scope.
216	
217	*Why.* Concept: solo-developer art load; PF-45: one calibration per kind.
218	*Edge notes.* Fallback if the silhouette test reads "gauge on a console" as the crewmate-reserved composition (ART 6.6 rule 2): a squarer, octagonal-chamfered arc authored once for both sizes (R-A2). If the terminal-fitting mount is rejected: dials only on MACHINE_PANEL mounts and the wall carries sight-glasses only. DIAL_L consumes 46 of 48 rows (a 1-px margin each side): it cannot be a console-face detail inside a cap-plus-face prop; this is a placement constraint routed to Layout and Derelict Authoring (IW-31).
219	
220	**IW-8. Instrument data and the calibration record (the answer to PF-45).**
221	*Rule.* Per instrument surface, a record in `assets/data/instruments/`: `instrument_id`; `gauge_kind` (DIAL | LINEAR | READOUT | GLYPH | FRAME); `size_class`; `quantity` (IW-9); `arc_deg` (DIAL; 0 for LINEAR); `needle_len_px` (DIAL) or `travel_px` (LINEAR meniscus travel); `value_lo`, `value_hi`, `lsb`, `unit_key`, `name_key` (the card label); `zones[]` as LS-7 band **names** mapped to a pattern class (D.2; the thresholds are derived at build time and never written into this data); `lie_surface_id` per corruptible surface (`<instrument_id>.needle`, `.glyph`, `.housing_glow`, `.machine_frame`; there is no `.readout` surface and the card has no id of its own: one ref carries one lie and one `Perceived`, so the card numeral is `displayed_value` of the `.needle` ref's `Perceived`, and `motion_mode` TICK and STALE apply to that numeral, checkpoint ruling C2); and `beyond_witness`, the flag set defined below, which is **derived from placement and quantity** and must equal the authored value (lint `BEYOND_WITNESS_MISMATCH`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The binding (`node_ref` or `room_key`, `mount`, `host_face` and, since the design review, `mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node`) is **placement data** authored in Layout and Derelict Authoring (IW-31). A missing or malformed record yields the honest path plus `lie_unrenderable` (PF-44), a **build failure** for any kind listed in `lie_targets.json`. Assets owed exactly as PF V.11: `mach_gauge_<loop>_alb.png` plus `_msk.png` with slices `glass`, `needle_edge`, `needle`; a `ui_` sheet with a `glass` slice for digit cells and card glass; `mach_<name>_<state>_alb.png`; `mach_lamp_<name>_lit` / `_unlit`; both honest state frames of every pair on **one sheet page** (advisor ruling R11; PF-45). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, answers Perception Filter PF-9 join)* **Join to Sanity's `subject_ref` `{stable_id, surface}` (SN-23).** `stable_id` is the module's stable id and equals the IW-8 `instrument_id` (lint: one-to-one). The surface enum maps to the facets above: 1 NEEDLE maps to `.needle`; 2 READOUT maps to the `.needle` facet of an instrument whose `gauge_kind` is READOUT (a digit-only instrument has no needle sprite, but its single lie facet is that ref, whose `displayed_value` is the numeral); 3 GLYPH to `.glyph`; 4 GLOW_SPRITE to `.housing_glow`; 5 MACHINE_SPRITE to `.machine_frame`. The ref's `quantity`, `node_ref` or `room_key` come from this record, never from the `subject_ref`. The record supplies both an OK and an alarm interval (PF-45) so the Filter can derive the GLIDE dial side. Lint `LIE_SURFACE_ENUM_MISMATCH`: a surface whose facet is absent from the record is a build failure.
222	*Definitions: mount, subject and `beyond_witness`.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text declared `beyond_witness` in {REMOTE, MAGNITUDE, TREND} without defining any value, and the manifest tagged instruments REMOTE that hang in the room they read.)* Placement splits the two places an instrument has. `mount_room` is the compartment in which the housing physically hangs; `subject_room` is the compartment holding what the reading is about (for a compartment ref the named `cid`; for a node ref the compartment that holds the node, found through `nodes_in(cid)`; for a POWER `loop_component` ref the compartment of its anchor node). `host_node` is the node whose own panel or prop carries the housing (none for a WALL_FACE mount) and `subject_node` is the bound node (none for a compartment ref). `hops(a, b)` is the shortest path over `neighbors(cid)` (LS-19) and `hops(a, a)` = 0. `beyond_witness` is a **set of flags computed by a lint from placement and quantity; nobody judges it, and the authored field must equal the computed set**:
223	
224	| Flag | Predicate (testable) | Reading for the player | Manifest example |

### Core Rules

*Conventions.* Rules are named `IW-n` (In-World); each states a **Rule** (what the player sees and the contract with neighbours), a **Why** and **Edge notes**. Formulas are `D.n` (Formulas section: D.1 needle angle, D.2 zone intervals, D.3 honest numeral, D.4 settle, D.5 tremor, D.6 card layout, D.7 legibility table, D.8 instrument budget, D.9 gleam edge, D.10 reduced-motion substitutes, D.11 linear instruments, D.12 `lsb` visibility lint). Conflicts are `K-n` (K-1..K-14 from the brief, K-15 and K-16 raised by the ux-designer, K-17 and K-18 raised in this stage); open questions `OQ-IW-n`. "(advisor ruling Rn)", "(checkpoint ruling Cn)" and "(Xn)" are provenance labels from the authoring run: the `rulings.md` they cite is not on disk and **no rulings digest exists in this document**; the rule each label governs is stated in the clause or rule that cites it, and a label is never the only statement of a rule *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the earlier claim that a digest at the end of Open Questions restates every ruling was false and is withdrawn); "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" marks a place where two specialists disagreed and this GDD picked one. Values that are this GDD's own and not yet registered are `[PLACEHOLDER]`; values quoted from a neighbour carry their owner and are never changed here. Implementation choices are tagged "-> ADR candidate" and kept out of the rules. **Chest-lamp sweep:** the beam origin is the per-facing chest point (PC); the lamp is hands-free; thrown Chemlight glowsticks (`#86B896`) light a gauge exactly as the beam does; no "hand lamp" wording appears anywhere in this document.

**Rule index.** Group A, what this system is: IW-1 ownership, IW-2 presentation-only, IW-3 lit-only readability, IW-4 housing pip, IW-5 reading source. Group B, the instrument family: IW-6 taxonomy, IW-7 dial template, IW-8 data and calibration record, IW-9 quantity set, IW-10 the needle element. Group C, honest motion: IW-11 continuous change and settle, IW-12 tremor, IW-13 motion-mode dispatch, IW-14 readouts, IW-15 zone bands. Group D, lying surfaces and state frames: IW-16 the gleam, IW-17 Module-Body Presenter, IW-18 WORN, IW-19 alarm mark, IW-20 sight-glass and linear instruments. Group E, the inspect view: IW-21 targeting, IW-22 card content, IW-23 placement, IW-24 lifecycle, IW-25 input and falsification, IW-26 parity. Group F, boundaries: IW-27 reduced motion, IW-28 never-do list, IW-29 manifest floors, IW-30 DEAD binding, IW-31 placement record, IW-32 sound, IW-33 pause and restore, IW-34 fallbacks, IW-35 flagged not edited, IW-36 legibility contract, IW-37 strings, IW-38 diagnostics.

#### Group A. What this system is

**IW-1. Ownership: module-body reading surfaces.**
*Rule.* In-World Instruments owns (a) every gauge, dial, level sight-glass and state glyph produced by the ship or a derelict, drawn as lit sprites on layer 0; (b) the inspect card on layer 2, the same instrument at HUD size; (c) the **Module-Body Presenter**: the selection among a module sheet's *honest* state frames and the drawing of the state glyph (IW-17). It owns no module art (Item DB `sprite_family` names the sheet and state tokens), no placement (Layout and Derelict Authoring), no behaviour of the module, and no decision about whether, when, for whom or by how much anything lies (Filter and Sanity). It never calls `true_value`. Every reading produced by the ship or a derelict is this GDD's; Suit & Equipment and HUD & Suit Layer own only suit-produced and hand-tool readings (advisor ruling R7, R24).
*Why.* IDX:39 and ART 7.0 ("the ship is an instrument": who produced the number decides where it is drawn). No sibling claims the presenter (DA:1340, FT:232, IA:920, PF:1461). DA:1571's row assigning "gauges and instruments reading authored systems" to "the suit and HUD" is a stale assignment, refreshed by its owner (K-4).
*Edge notes.* The index has no row naming the module presenter (K-11): flagged to the producer, not edited here (IW-35).

**IW-2. Presentation-only, zero registrations.**
*Rule.* Instruments are `PRESENTATION` subscribers (KRN:106-110; PIPE PR-8). They read `SIM` and `PERCEPTION_OUT` views and write only CanvasItem, Material, Light2D, particle and audio-request state; never a block, a command, a hook or a mutator. A notification is a dirty mark; reading and drawing happen in the render callback; placement is integer base px; nothing here can cause a tick. The card is **not** an `INPUT_SURFACE`: it issues no commands. The Controller's Adapter (an `INPUT_SURFACE`) owns the `inspect_card` context and publishes a presentation-local signal `{context, inspect_ref}` (registry: `inspect_card_context_signal`) that Instruments subscribe to (IW-25). Instruments register no block, hook, mutator, dirty key or persisted field (advisor ruling R22; K-1).
*Why.* PR-8 rule 1 (PIPE:188): `INPUT_SURFACE` only "if it also issues commands — the HUD's prompts do not; the chart table does" (PIPE's example only: per Chart Table CT-27, the chart table holds the `INPUT_SURFACE` class for VS-B and submits nothing at MVP). Instruments submit nothing.
*Edge notes.* Refresh owed by the Controller: PC-16 (PC:147: "an `INPUT_SURFACE` of In-World Instruments"), PC:77's purpose column ("Interaction's inspect verb", contradicting IA-38), PC:210 row 10 (K-1, K-12).

**IW-3. Lit-only readability: "What You Light, You Can Read".**
*Rule.* A world gauge is readable exactly as far as the world lighting makes its pixels visible: Instruments do **not** gate the drawing of a world gauge on `lit(ref)`; the lit renderer and the HullSurface material make an unlit face dark. Two things are gated on the Emitter State bit `lit(ref)` (hysteresis `LIT_ON_PM` 150 / `LIT_OFF_PM` 120, no dwell; owner technical-artist; EM-22): the **inspect prompt** (Interaction's, IW-21) and the **inspect card** (IW-24). No instrument is an emitter and no gauge is a lantern. Mechanical gauges need no power to be read at MVP, so a dead loop's gauge shows its reading as soon as light reaches it. Thrown Chemlight glowsticks and fixtures light a gauge as the beam does.
*Why.* P3: reading spends light. Gating the card by the sim bit and the face by the renderer keeps one source of light truth each (ART 7.0 "unreadable until lit"; LO:436; EM:864).
*Edge notes.* Between `LIT_OFF_PM` and `LIT_ON_PM` the face may be dimly visible while the card is refused: intended (precision costs more light than a glance). Gauge motion is updated whether or not the face is lit (cheap, and a face entering the beam shows its current needle on its first lit frame); the gleam is "lit with its host" and needs no lit query (PF-16). The face is never shown or hidden by `lit(ref)` in code, so the 150/120 hysteresis cannot make a face flash at a pool edge (HR-13); only the prompt and the card are lit-gated, and the card needs a fresh press to reopen. Whether a gauge needs power at a later tier is OQ-IW-11.

**IW-4. Self-emission is a non-readable housing pip, and the pip is corruptible.**
*Rule.* "A running loop's gauge is faintly lit by its own emission" (ART 7.0) is realised as a small loop-hue **housing pip** (size `[PLACEHOLDER]`, 4x2 art px proposed by the art-director, 2x2 by the ux-designer; OQ-IW-12) on the emissive layer (mask bit 2, casts no light, exposes nothing; LO-14, LO:225). It exists only while the bound subject's `served_pm` > 0, lets the player *find* a running gauge in the dark, and does **not** make the face readable and does **not** make `lit(ref)` true. It is drawn through the `HOUSING_GLOW(ref)` ref, so it is stage-2 corruptible: finding a gauge by its pip is not proof its loop runs. Its emission is capped at or below fixture glow and well below the beam (`PIP_EMIT_MAX`, set by the Lighting spike, ART 8.12); the hull/integrity loop has no pip (it has no running medium) (advisor ruling R21; K-6).
*Why.* Keeps `lit(ref)`, the card, Sanity's lit-entry and P3 consistent without adding emitters or an Emitter State change (LO-14's channel rule: "a lamp housing's own emissive sprite ... read the Filter channel and may lie").
*Edge notes.* The pip carries **presence or absence only** ("something here is running"); loop identity is the housing's fitting silhouette (IW-7), so the hue-removed test is met by silhouette and by the pip's on/off state. The fixture lamp's brightness from `served_pm` is consequence channel and is never confused with the pip, which casts no pool.

**IW-5. Reading source: one pull per instrument per frame; never cache; never read truth.**
*Rule.* In the render callback each on-screen instrument in a loaded section obtains its displayed value with exactly one `perceived(ref, viewer)` call (PF-7), `viewer` being the local seat's `PlayerId`; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* one **`InstrumentPresenter` per instrument** is the sole caller of `perceived()` for its ref and the sole owner of the settle, tremor, dwell and notch scalars, and the wall node and the card are views of the frame index and digits it publishes once per frame (the Filter's `(ref, viewer, frame)` memo is the backstop; ADR candidate, X-6). An instrument never stores a `Perceived` record across frames, never addresses the Filter by `peer_id` (PF-10), and never calls `true_value`, `summary()` (a ship-status read), `power_use()` (Attention's stimulus) or `can_join()`. It may read `read_view` only for **non-value** inputs: the tremor predicate (IW-12), module frame selection and WORN (IW-17, IW-18), the alarm predicate (IW-19), and binding validity (IW-30). Those reads are refreshed once per Graph step (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6), not per frame, and never feed a displayed value. The needle target is `displayed_pm`. The honest tremor offset is multiplied by `tremor_weight_pm / 1000` from the same pull (IW-12, D.5). The presentation-local scalars now also include `env_hold` (the tremor envelope latched at the first non-HONEST frame; discarded at `tremor_weight_pm` 0, `hard_start`, cull, cut and restore), which is drawing state like the settle triple, never a cached `Perceived`. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* An instrument that is off-screen or in an unloaded section pulls nothing; on its first pull after being culled it **snaps** to `displayed_pm` with no settle and no interpolation from stale history (history older than one Graph step is meaningless, and a settle on re-entry would be a motion with no world cause, P1) (advisor ruling R18).
*Why.* PF-8: the record never contains the truth while a lie is active; caching would let a stale record outlive a lie's end. R18 and PF-3: only the Filter wraps a true value.
*Edge notes.* Presentation-local scalars (the settle triple, `prev_honest_pm` and the rest, window and reversal-dwell scalars of IW-11, tremor onset and decay timestamps, `env_hold`, the numeral throttle timestamp) are derived drawing state, not cached `Perceived` records: each is a pure function of values the player was already shown, none is read by another system, all are discarded on restore, cull and camera cut. **CONFLICT K-17 (new): LSG:998 and LS-20 (LSG:201) (locked) say "gauges read `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles" (LS-20: "Instruments and Audio poll `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles")**, which contradicts R18/PF-3 (a gauge never reads a value from `read_view`). This GDD follows R18 and PF-3: value reads go only through `perceived`; the "smooth needles" of LSG:998 and LS-20 is delivered by IW-11's interpolation, not by a value read. The Graph's own sentences are routed to its owner as a refresh. Related: the honest path carries no previous value, which IW-11 answers with the local scalar `prev_honest_pm` (K-17, checkpoint ruling C14).

#### Group B. The instrument family

**IW-6. Taxonomy: wall instrument kinds and the card's numeral; one definition at two scales.**
*Rule.* Every instrument is one data definition (`assets/data/instruments/<instrument_id>`, IW-8) rendered by one scene definition at two scales: the wall or panel node (layer 0, art px x `k`) and the card (layer 2, HUD art px x `H`). The kinds:

| Kind | `gauge_kind` | World form (no numerals, ART 3.1) | Card form | Motion signatures | Lie reach (SN-16) | Sizes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dial | DIAL | open 240-degree arc strip on a chamfered rectangular housing; separate pivoted needle; zone bands; hub | same dial at HUD px, label, numeral | settle, tremor, glide (with wander) | needle: stage 1 | DIAL_L, DIAL_S (IW-7) |
| Level sight-glass | LINEAR | vertical glass tube, fluid column, meniscus bead, side zone strip and ticks | same glass, label, numeral | settle, tremor, glide (linear branch, D.11) | meniscus: stage 1 | one size at MVP, `travel_px` 50 `[PLACEHOLDER]` (IW-20) |
| Numeral | READOUT | **none in the world** | digit cells in a glass-edged well | honest step per real change; lie: continuous tick or stale hold (PF-18) | numeral: stage 1 | card only |
| State glyph | GLYPH | 8x8 lens mark on a module housing; two shape-coded frames (run, stop); no flow mark, no loop hue | not carried | frame swap (no needle motion) | stage 2 | 8x8 |
| Machine frame | FRAME | the module's own state frames (IW-17) | not carried | frame cut, rotor cadence | stage 3 (SPRITE_SWAP) | module cell (96x96) |

Housing glow frames (the lamp lit/unlit pair) and the pip (IW-4) ride the `HOUSING_GLOW` ref (stage 2). The stage-1 "readout" of SN-16 is the card's numeral, which is `displayed_value` of the `.needle` ref's `Perceived` (the digit tick of PF-18 acts there; TICK and STALE govern the numeral only, IW-13); it is not a second lie surface. A wall gauge carries no digit. The SN-16 "readout" wording is routed to Sanity and the `motion_mode` field description and PF-18 to the Filter as a wording refresh (checkpoint ruling C2).
*(orchestrator ruling: the ux-designer proposed an 8-pip drum ladder as an in-world "digital readout"; the art-director and ui-programmer proposed card-only. Card-only is adopted: a pip ladder is a numeral in disguise against ART 3.1, doubles the asset set for a solo developer and adds a lie surface with no witness value beyond the needle. The battery-stock instruments become DIAL_S `stock` dials in the manifest, IW-29.)*
*Why.* One calibration for the Filter (PF-45), one test set, one art load; the card is "the same instrument magnified" by construction.
*Edge notes.* A decorative gauge that carries no remote, magnitude or trend information beyond its local witness is forbidden (IW-29). The loop identity of an instrument is never carried by dial geometry (IW-7).

**IW-7. Dial template family: two authored sizes, one arc.**
*Rule.* All dials use `arc_deg` 240 (open sector at the bottom; the arc runs -120 to +120 degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock). Two authored sizes (registry: `dial_size_class`): **DIAL_L** `needle_len_px` 24 in a 96x48 prop cell and **DIAL_S** `needle_len_px` 18 in a 48x48 cell. Both are at or above `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` 16 (owner: this GDD; value unchanged, range 14.3-32) and glide-eligible: `rate_floor` = max(0.5, 28.6 / `needle_len_px`) = 1.19 deg/s at 24 and 1.59 deg/s at 18, inside the 0.5-2.0 band (PF-13, PF-17). Loop identity is the housing's fitting silhouette (ART 3.4, 7.2 table) plus the running-only pip, never dial geometry or face hue. Geometry (art px; pivot at the arc centre; band inner radius = needle length + 1; one geometry set, fixed by checkpoint ruling C5; the pixel mock S-A1 confirms the DIAL_S bezel only):

| Size | Needle | Band inner r | Band thickness | Outer r | Arc width (2 x outer r) | Arc height (1.5 x outer r) | Housing (DIAL_L bezel 2 px, DIAL_S bezel 1 px, each side) | Cell | Cell margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DIAL_L | 24 | 25 | 3 | 28 | 56 | 42 | 60 x 46 | 96x48 | 36 px horizontal, 2 px vertical |
| DIAL_S | 18 | 19 | 3 | 22 | 44 | 33 | 46 x 35 (bezel 1 px each side) | 48x48 | 1 px each side horizontally, 13 px vertically in total |

*Arithmetic.* A 240-degree arc centred on 12 o'clock reaches its full width at the 3 and 9 o'clock points (|x| = r) and its lowest point at the end stops (y = r cos 120 = -0.5 r), so height = r (above the pivot) + 0.5 r (below) = 1.5 r. Needle stroke is 2 art px (HR-12: a stroke is at least 2 screen px at every `k`). The outer radius is the band's inner radius plus its thickness: DIAL_L 25 + 3 = 28 (arc 2 x 28 = 56 wide, 1.5 x 28 = 42 high, housing 56 + 4 = 60 by 42 + 4 = 46 with a 2 px bezel), DIAL_S 19 + 3 = 22 (arc 2 x 22 = 44 wide, 1.5 x 22 = 33 high, housing 44 + 2 = 46 by 33 + 2 = 35 with a 1 px bezel). The DIAL_S band is **3 rows** because IW-15 needs three patterns (solid, hatched, notched) that can be told apart; a 2-row band could not carry them. The **stress predicate** (MVP) is any of: (i) an active hazard-mode FailureDescriptor on the bound node, mode in {1 LEAK, 2 SHORT, 3 OVERHEAT, 4 FREEZE, 5 BREACH, 7 OVERLOAD} (LS-11), with `sev` >= `TREMOR_SEV_MIN` (1), read through `failures(filter)`; never mode 10 WORN, 6 STARVE, 8 SEVERED, 9 SCRAM or **27 PATCH_WEEP** (a patched subject's steady weep, LS-11 row 27: `hp_cap < HP_FULL` with no mode 1-9 live, no `intensity_pm`; it is a consequence-channel witness of the patch, not a stress) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and never a compartment band descriptor (ATMO_COLD / HOT / THIN / DECOMP 20-23, AIRFLOW 24, PUDDLE 25): a band is a state, not a stress (advisor final-review amendment to R9: `warn_elapsed` is > 0 for every sev-1 subject, LSG D.11, so it is not a tremor input); (ii) an active OVERLOAD (mode 7) descriptor on a CABLE of the bound loop component, through `failures(filter)` (LSG:127); (iii) an active `SEAL_STRAIN` descriptor on an OPENING of the bound compartment, or a `LEAK` or `BREACH` descriptor on a HULL_SEGMENT or SEAM bounding it (subjects found through `nodes_in(cid)` and `neighbors(cid)`; read through `failures(filter)`); the subject lists of (i)-(iii) are precomputed at section load and recomputed only on a topology dirty key (`T`, `SEC/<id>`), never per frame. (iv) **`stress_active(section_id)`, off by default** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the MVP predicate is (i)-(iii) only, and (iv) is read only if the knob `TREMOR_USE_SECTION_STRESS` is true (default **false**, registered in Tuning Knobs); (K-13 resolved: the Graph now publishes the pure query, LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27; section stress is `stress_pm` = `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` 2000 while `step_no < stress_until_step`, set by M17 STRESS for `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` 600) for an instrument in that section. **(iv) is provisional and off:** M17 STRESS has one caller, Attention, which this rule forbids as a tremor driver (a tremor driven by it would make an instrument show Attention, which the header and IW-28 forbid, AT-17), and AT C1 reads a needle moved by real STRESS damage as a consequence and not a tell; the creative-director's position is that (iv) as written is a pillar-level conflict, so it stays off until the Attention owner and the creative-director confirm the contrary reading (OQ-IW-38); with the knob false the predicate is (i)-(iii) and `stress_active` is not read by Instruments. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The predicate is refreshed once per Graph step (IW-5). Tremor is never driven by Attention, sanity, a timer or a lie. A fading tremor is the honest tremor already in progress, not a lie's. It is positional, not luminous (HR-13 exemption; shown on the card as well, suppressed under `reduced_motion`, D96) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The tremor is STARTED and its predicate is read only when `motion_mode` is HONEST (advisor ruling R9; AT-17, AT:1415 C1). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Perception Filter publishes `tremor_weight_pm` and BREATH, PF-8, PF-17)* **Onset of a lie: a running tremor fades, it does not stop.** Instruments read `tremor_weight_pm` (int 0..1000, the tenth `Perceived` field, PF-8; 1000 on every HONEST frame; read from the same single `perceived()` pull as `displayed_pm`, never computed or cached here). In the first non-HONEST frame the presenter latches `env_hold := env` of the last HONEST frame (0 if no tremor was running) and from then on (a) no new tremor starts and no onset ramp runs in any non-HONEST frame (the predicate is not read; a flag cannot be set in a non-HONEST frame), (b) env stays `env_hold` (no rise, no decay of its own; the fade is carried by `tremor_weight_pm` alone), (c) the drawn offset is the D.5 offset multiplied by `tremor_weight_pm / 1000`, which falls linearly from 1000 on the first ACTIVE frame to 0 over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (Filter-owned, := `WANDER_ONSET_S`, 1.0 s `[PLACEHOLDER]`) and stays 0 until CLEAR, and (d) the flag clears and `env_hold` is discarded when `tremor_weight_pm` reaches 0, on `hard_start`, cull, camera cut and restore (so a restore mid-fade shows no tremor: Instruments never start one), and at the first HONEST frame after the lie (CLEAR): the predicate is then re-read and, if stress still holds, a fresh `TREMOR_ONSET_MS` ramp starts from env 0; `env_hold` is never carried across CLEAR. The **settle triple and the reduced-motion notch are the opposite: they are cleared at once** in the first non-HONEST frame (IW-11 (e), IW-27); under `reduced_motion` the tremor is not drawn, so there is nothing to fade and only the immediate notch clearing applies. Why the fade is `tremor_weight_pm` and not the 600 ms `TREMOR_DECAY_MS`: the tremor fades out over exactly the window in which the Filter's wander fades in (`TREMOR_BLEND_S` := `WANDER_ONSET_S`), so the onset second is never still (PF-17, AC-PF-46 bounds the onset rest on this); letting the predicate go false at onset would decay the envelope in about 0.3 s and leave about 0.7 s of near-stillness, and a tremor that stops dead at lie onset is itself a tell.
268	**On the card (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D96 — the card shows the honest tremor, suppressed under `reduced_motion`; K-18 resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.** The card shows the same honest tremor as its wall gauge (parity, IW-26; the same fade at lie onset, from the same presenter state and the same `tremor_weight_pm`; the amplitude is +-`TREMOR_AMP_PX` HUD art px, never scaled by the card multiple). With `reduced_motion` on, the tremor is suppressed on the card exactly as on the wall gauge and the held stress notch pair of IW-27 and D.10 shows in its place (two Hull Grey squares on the Ground plate above the dial) while the predicate holds and the reading is HONEST, so the stress tell never depends on motion for a player who has asked for less of it. The earlier objection (HR-13 says "no HUD shake"; ART:984 flags tremor's positional-not-luminous status as unconfirmed) is answered by this suppression and by the card frame, plate and keycaps never moving; the former fallback (the held notch on the card in all modes) is retired unless the user declines this default. Further accessibility-specialist advice is welcome when Accessibility Settings is designed, but nothing here waits on it.
269	*Why.* P2: the honest tremor is the instrument's share of the 10-30 s tell and is a real consequence the player can trace. "A needle moved by STRESS damage is a consequence, not a tell Attention drives" (AT C1). Because a tremor is only ever started on an honest reading (a running one fades at a lie's onset, it is never begun or driven by the lie), "shake = real" is a rule the game never breaks. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*
270	*Edge notes.* A patched or WORN subject carries only mode 10 WORN (LS-11, LS-23), so it does not tremble; its `warn_elapsed` is > 0 (LSG D.11), which is why `warn_elapsed` is not a tremor input. `alarm_eligible` (`sev` >= 3, LS-13) is not a tremor input; tremor begins at the first physical stress, always before the alarm class (`W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10 is the Graph's). If the predicate flaps at Graph-step rate, tremor flaps with it (10 Hz worst case); `TREMOR_HOLD_S` (default 0) is the playtest remedy. Tremor's perceptibility at `k` 1 on the largest field is marginal (D.7); the design accepts it, since the tell is for a player standing at the instrument. **Instrument tremor is never the only tell (stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 6).** It is this system's share of the P2 10-30 s tell and P2 is carried by several channels: every stress source in predicates (i)-(iii) above must also have a sound tell or a world-witness tell owned by Adaptive Audio or Failure & Trail (strain creak, hiss, drip, spark or frost, per the consequence channel), so zooming out to `k` 1, or standing outside the light, never removes the warning. This is a cross-owner requirement checked by AC-IW-106 and routed to Adaptive Audio and Failure & Trail.

272	**IW-13. Motion-mode dispatch.**
273	*Rule.* The Filter's `motion_mode` (HONEST, GLIDE, TICK, STALE, BREATH, RETURN) is the only switch: *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*
274	
275	| `motion_mode` | Needle / meniscus | Numeral (card) | Settle | Tremor | Stress notch (RM) | Drawn value from |
276	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
277	| HONEST | `displayed_pm` through IW-11 and IW-12 | steps once per real change (throttled, IW-14) | yes | yes if predicate (`tremor_weight_pm` 1000) | yes if predicate | Instruments |
278	| GLIDE | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | continuous tick follows | no | no new tremor; a tremor running at onset fades by `tremor_weight_pm` (D.5) | no (cleared that frame) | the Filter's value; Instruments draw it |
279	| TICK | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | continuous tick, `T_tick` (PF-18) | no | same as GLIDE | no | same |
280	| STALE | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | held digits | no | same as GLIDE | no | same |
281	| RETURN | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory: the rate-limited follower to truth) | follows | no | same as GLIDE (`tremor_weight_pm` is 0 once its blend is over and stays 0 until CLEAR) | no | same |
282	| BREATH *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: PF-8, PF-15 table, PF L335, L554)* | none: the surface is a static pair (state glyph, lamp-housing glow, machine state) with no needle; `frame_override` (the other honest frame of the pair, IW-17) is drawn and held still for the whole lie | none | no | no (a tremor exists only on a DIAL or LINEAR needle, IW-12, so none can be running; `tremor_weight_pm` is ignored) | no | `frame_override` from the Filter; the gleam breathes between `floor_eff` and `AMP_MAX_PM` over 4 to 6 s, drawn from `leak_amplitude_pm` exactly as IW-16 already draws any amplitude (no new behaviour) |

284	An honest gauge never glides; a lie never settles and never starts a tremor (a tremor already running at onset fades through `tremor_weight_pm`, IW-12, D.5); the instrument never infers a lie, it only obeys the mode. (PF-7 edge note, PF-17; orchestrator ruling R8 of the Filter run) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*
285	*Why.* If Instruments could decide, the player could read the truth from which animation applies: a P4 oracle.
286	*Edge notes.* The card has the identical dispatch (IW-26). A numeral-only READOUT (`gauge_kind` READOUT, no needle) lying FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL arrives as STALE (not BREATH) with its gleam breathing through `leak_amplitude_pm` (PF L334, L789); BREATH is the record mode of static-pair refs only (`.glyph`, `.housing_glow`, `.machine_frame`). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* **TICK and STALE are modes of the card numeral only** (checkpoint ruling C2): a wall gauge carries no digit (IW-6), and a `lie_displayed_value` lie moves a FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL needle toward its zone and never holds it. No lying needle rests: whatever the numeral's mode, the needle draws the Filter's trajectory, which never rests (PF-17), so the wall gauge keeps its motion mode while the card is closed (PF-8, HR-5). The numeral's STALE hold is a card-visible mode of the same lie, not a second one; the gleam and the motion mode remain mandatory and only the sound is droppable (PF-8).

288	**IW-14. The numeral: honest ticking, the throttle, and who owns the scheduler.**
289	*Rule.* Numerals exist only on the card (IW-6). An honest numeral steps once per real change of `displayed_value` at the quantity's `lsb`, never tweens and never counts up; a transition is a digit-glyph substitution in tabular cells (fixed width, slashed zero) of only the cells whose glyph changed, and never inverts a plate (PF-18; HR-13 is then checkable per cell). Honest transitions are throttled to the same ceiling as lying ones: the card's numeral updates on the HUD's shared **hold grid** `HONEST_TICK_MS` (owner HUD & Suit Layer, HS-14, pinned 500 ms and ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions, D91 iii) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the 400-500 range is withdrawn, the HUD's window-feasibility check leaves 30 ticks as the only feasible grid, HS-47; PF-18's 334 is the bound without the beacon share and is not used here), at most `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 transitions per rolling second; no second constant is registered here. At each grid boundary the numeral shows the **then-current** step (it may skip steps, never queued, never faded; it never shows a value the room did not have). The card's honest numeral changes only on the HUD's shared `HONEST_TICK_MS` grid boundary and adds no luminance event of its own (HS-47); a boundary at which no card digit changes is not an event; when the HUD's grid-skip rule skips a boundary the card shows the then-latest step at the next one, so honest numeral lag is at most `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS`. A lying numeral is the Filter's: a continuous tick or a stale hold under the shared scheduler `T_tick` = max(`LIE_TICK_MS` 400, N_r x 334) (400 / 668 / 1002 / 1336 ms for N_r 1..4; the 334 ms stagger floor keeps any closed 1 s window at or under `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3) (PF-18, registry `lying_digit_tick_schedule`); Instruments only draw the received digits. Formatting is integer-only: the displayed value is `displayed_value` converted by the quantity table (IW-9) with no float formatting; a temperature that rounds to -0 shows "0"; a value beyond the span shows the clamped bound with no "<" mark (a "<" would be a second reading); the format never reveals more precision than `lsb`. **`lsb` visibility lint:** for a lie-eligible dial, `lsb` must be fine enough that the digit changes at least every `T_VIS_MAX_S` during a glide at the floor rate (otherwise a lying numeral looks stale and the tri-modal rule loses a mode on the card): `p_o2` is therefore shown in kPa with one decimal (`lsb` 1 dkPa), not in whole kPa (D.12). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
290	*Why.* ART 7.3 (honest numerals tick); HR-13 (no luminance change faster than 3 Hz); PF-18.
291	*Edge notes.* **CONFLICT K-16 (raised by the ux-designer):** locked fact 21 / ART 7.3 say an honest numeral ticks "one step per real change, never a tween", while HR-13 and `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 cap digit-glyph substitutions at 3 per second; a breach would exceed the cap if every step were shown. This GDD throttles and shows the then-current step, exactly as HUD & Suit Layer does for its own honest numerals (HS-14 amends the same locked rule, and its K8 row accepts the amendment); exempting honest ticks from the ceiling is rejected because a photosensitive player gains nothing from the distinction. Honest grid boundaries on the card are not counted in the Filter's `N_r` (which counts lying readouts only); the combined HUD budget (card numeral plus suit numerals plus lying readouts) is the HUD's arbiter HS-47, which itself records an open counting unit and an ASK to the Filter and the accessibility-specialist when lying digits at `N_r` 2 or more fill the ceiling *(OQ-IW-9: HS-47 states that the card's honest numeral shares the HUD's grid boundary and adds no event; the open counting unit is HUD CF-HS-10)*. The digit mechanism (glyph-cell substitution from a `ui_` atlas versus a text node) is -> ADR candidate; tabular numerals, slashed-zero shaping and integer-scale snapping of a vector font are `[UNV]` for the pinned build and ART 7.1 makes them asset-test requirements. The same honest-digit mechanism is offered as a reusable component to HUD & Suit Layer for the field-check reading (IW-35).
292	
293	**IW-15. Zone bands are coded by pattern first, hue second.**
294	*Rule.* Every dial and linear instrument carries zone bands derived **at build time** from LS-7 band names (D.2), never typed as numbers in instrument data. A band has a pattern class: SOLID (normal-class bands: `NORMAL`, `COMFORT`), HATCHED (caution: `THIN`, `LOW`, `COOL`, `HOT`, `FROST`), NOTCHED (critical: `HYPOXIC`, `ANOXIC`, `DECOMP`, `VACUUM`, `SCORCH`, `FREEZING`, `DEEP_COLD`; overload for `load`); the three must be distinguishable from each other at 25 % scale in greyscale (the hue-removed test). Gauge faces carry no loop hue (identity is the fitting silhouette and, while running, the pip); Alarm Red is never a zone colour (a static red band on every dial would make red common and decorative, violating ART 4.1). A zone narrower than `ZONE_MIN_ARC_PX` (6 art px of arc, D.2) fails a build lint: the instrument must use a larger size class or merge bands in data. The needle position is geometry; the needle is **not** coloured by the Graph's hysteretic `band_*` fields (advisor ruling R11).
295	*Why.* Hue-removed readability (ART 4.7, HR-5 test); LS-7 is the single source of bands.
296	*Edge notes.* Because LS-7 bands carry hysteresis (`H_P` 5 dkPa, `H_T` 500 mC) while dial zones are static intervals, the needle can sit inside the NORMAL zone while the Graph's `band_o2` still reads THIN: the dial is a continuous reading and no consumer compares them. The exact authored patterns (hatched dashes, split-rail, notched teeth) at a 3-row DIAL_S band are the pixel mock's to confirm (OQ-IW-3).
