**IW-9. The quantity set and ref addressing.**
*Rule.* The closed MVP quantity set (registry: `instrument_quantity`); each row names the Graph source, unit, span, `lsb` and band family. Bands are LS-7 and LSG D.9, consumed by name and never redefined; spans are this GDD's gauge spans `[PLACEHOLDER]` pending the Graph's LS-26 nominals:

| `quantity` | Graph source (`read_view`) | Unit shown | `value_lo` .. `value_hi` | `lsb` | Zone family | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `p_o2` | `compartment(cid).p_o2` | kPa (value / 10), one decimal | 0 .. 300 dkPa | 1 dkPa | LS-7 `p_o2` bands | DIAL |
| `P` | `compartment(cid).P` | kPa, whole | 0 .. 1100 dkPa | 10 dkPa | LS-7 `P` bands | DIAL |
| `T` | `compartment(cid).T` | whole degrees C (mC / 1000) | -60000 .. 90000 mC | 1000 mC | LS-7 `T` bands (7 bands) | DIAL_L only |
| `stock` | `node(id).stock_pm` (the Graph's `⌊1000 × stock / capacity⌋`, capacity = the def's `cap_ml`, `BATT_CELL` or the O2_TANK template maximum; `true_value` kind `stock_pm`, LS-19 additions) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | percent | 0 .. 1000 permille | 10 permille | none (an empty-end tick only) | LINEAR (tank, reservoir) or DIAL_S (battery) |
| `load` | the Graph's `load_pm` `true_value` kind for a POWER `loop_component` (**requested**, specified below; this is not LSG `rho`, which is per edge and built from served-power sums) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | percent of supply | 0 .. 1250 permille | 10 permille | high edge at 1000 pm is this GDD's calibration (the brownout, D.6 `sat` < 1000), not an LS-7 band | DIAL |
| `strain` (held out of the MVP manifest, provisional) | `node(id).hp` inverted | an engineering-unit key, never a percent | 0 .. 10000 bp | 250 bp (the dirty quantum) | `HP_OK` 7000 / `HP_FAIL` 3000 edges | DIAL |

*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The `load` reading is a Graph-published quantity, not an Instruments derivation.** LS-19 publishes `supply` and `demand` as `true_value` kinds and calls their ratio "Instruments' own reading", but the Filter can only wrap a `true_value` and IW-5 forbids Instruments deriving a value outside the Filter, so a derived `load` had no lie path and no dirty-key quantum. The chosen path is **(a): the Graph publishes `load_pm` as a `true_value` kind** (request OQ-IW-20; cross-GDD note to the Life-Support Graph). Specification: `load_pm` = 0 when `supply` = 0, and `min(1250, floor(1000 x demand / supply))` otherwise; the clamp to the span belongs to the publisher, so `displayed_pm` is always inside 0..1000 and `diag.instr_pm_clamped` stays a defect counter. **Three bus cases, no longer folded into one pegged reading.** *Dead* (`supply` 0, `demand` > 0): the needle rests at the low stop, there is no housing pip (the pip needs `served_pm` > 0), the lamps are dark and the hum is silent, so the player is told that nothing is carried and not that the bus is overloaded. *Idle* (`supply` > 0, `demand` 0): the same low stop with the pip lit, so dead and idle are told apart by the pip and the lamps and not by the needle. *Loaded or overloaded* (`supply` > 0): 1..1250, with the NOTCHED stop from 1000. **Dirty cadence:** `load_pm` rides the loop key `L/<loop>/<anchor>` with a quantum of `LOAD_QUANTUM_PERMILLE` 20 (proposed; Graph-owned like the other LS-20 quanta; 16 pm of the 0..1250 span, 1.6 px on DIAL_L). The Filter wraps `load_pm` like any other kind: a lie moves the needle on the Filter's glide band and carries the full tri-modal leak. Until the Graph grants `load_pm`, `inst_engine_bus_load` is not buildable as a lie target (it is TRUTH-default by floor (i) in any case, so no manifest count moves). **Interim path (b), if the Graph declines:** the Filter's wrap derives the identical expression from `true_value(supply)` and `true_value(demand)` of the same component inside its one wrap point and states how lie and leak apply to the derived value; Instruments never derive.

`strain` is held out because a hull-condition dial risks becoming a condition bar in disguise (BS-6, FT-4, IDB): it ships only if the Graph confirms a physical stress quantity that is not `hp` (OQ-IW-5). Coolant **temperature** is not a quantity: no `read_view` field carries it (`T` is a compartment atmosphere value), so coolant instruments are level (`stock`) readings only until the Graph publishes one. **Ref addressing.** A node-bound instrument uses `GRAPH_NODE(kind, id)`; a room instrument uses `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` (registry `perceived_query` `ref_union`; the Filter adopted the `quantity` term at the 2026-10-27 consistency pass, PF-9), so two lie-eligible compartment instruments in one room are distinct in PF-7's `(ref, viewer, frame)` memo. **Adopted by the Filter (PF-9, OQ-PF-29):** the `quantity` term and the LINEAR branch. **Confirmed by the Graph (LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27):** the `true_value(kind, id)` kinds are `p_o2`, `P`, `T` (compartment), `stock_pm` (node), `supply` and `demand` (POWER component), plus `hp` for diagnostics, and the former fallback of one lie-eligible compartment instrument per room is retired. Two instruments with the same `(subject, quantity)` still share one ref and so one lie, which would not be a second opinion; the lint `INSTR_QUANTITY_COLLISION` therefore fails the build for a duplicated `(subject_room or subject_node, quantity)` pair. `load_pm` is requested (above). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (advisor ruling R12; K-5, resolved)
*Why.* The registry formula `atmosphere_derive` lists this GDD in its `referenced_by`; the Graph does not enumerate `true_value` kinds anywhere (grep of LSG and PF found none).
*Edge notes.* The `T` gauge in `cryo_bay` is lie-eligible beside the `p_o2` dial now that the fallback is retired (IW-29) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The ui-programmer's alternative ids (`p_total`, `temp`, `bus_load`, `store_level`) are not used; the ids mirror the Graph's field names (orchestrator ruling).

**IW-10. The needle element.**
*Rule.* A needle is a **separate pivoted element** (never part of the face art) whose tip is placed on whole art pixels at integer base-px positions with nearest-neighbour sampling, 2 art px thick; the tip moves in whole art pixels: one pixel step corresponds to 9.95 pm on DIAL_L and 13.3 pm on DIAL_S (D.1). No instrument draws any element with a drawn line or an anti-aliased edge: the pinned engine's `CanvasItem` line drawing carries no antialiasing feather in 4.7 (`[REF]` breaking-changes.md), so a drawn needle would be thinner than authored and PF-45's separate-needle requirement unmet. Zone bands, ticks and bezel arcs are authored sprites baked into the face at build time, never drawn at runtime. The needle's wander (Filter-supplied) and tremor (IW-12) are real whole-pixel tip flips, not shimmer.
*Why.* 4.7 engine fact; PF-45; ART 7.3.
*Edge notes.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Decision (baseline): pre-rendered needle frames indexed by the rounded tip pixel, drawn with NEAREST filtering and no runtime rotation.** The build tool enumerates the distinct rounded tip positions along the arc (about 100 on DIAL_L and 76 on DIAL_S: the arc length `needle_len_px` x 4.19) and bakes one 2-px needle frame per tip pixel; a frame index is the only thing the presenter changes. The wall needle and the card needle read the **same frame index, computed once per frame by the instrument's presenter**, in a fixed order (read `perceived()`, advance the scalars, compute the tip pixel, publish one index), so wall and card parity holds by construction. A runtime-rotated `Sprite2D` stays the fallback only if spike S-A3 (OQ-IW-7, `[UNV]`: no engine-reference file covers rotation under NEAREST at `k` 1..8) shows the frame strip over budget. The Filter-facing contract is identical either way (pivot at the dial centre, `needle_len_px` the authored tip radius). A card needle is the same angle set as the wall needle, not a finer rotation (IW-26). The ADR is X-6 item 7.

#### Group C. Honest motion

**IW-11. Continuous change and the honest settle (closed form).**
*Rule.* Everything in this rule applies **only when `motion_mode` is HONEST**. (a) **Continuous change.** Honest samples of `displayed_pm` arrive when the Filter's honest memo is invalidated (an LS-20 quantum crossing, at most once per Graph step, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6); while the Graph value sits inside one quantum there is no sample. **For MVP the honest needle's resolution is the LS-20 quantum** (checkpoint ruling C14): each instrument keeps one presentation-local scalar `prev_honest_pm` (the scalar that extends the triple of (c), beside the native-unit `prev_honest_native` that D.3 formats the card numeral from *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*); a new honest sample is drawn as a ramp from `prev_honest_pm` to the new accepted `target_pm` (the sample after the reversal dwell of (b); equal to `displayed_pm` unless a one-quantum reversal is still held) over one Graph step (100 ms) through the single PR-8 rule-5 interpolator (`tick_alpha`), with no overshoot and no extrapolation, and the needle then rests. The drawn value therefore lags the true value by at most one Graph step plus the quantum, except for a genuine one-quantum reversal, which the reversal dwell of (b) holds for `INSTR_REVERSAL_DWELL_STEPS` more steps (at most 500 ms in all) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the consequence channel tolerates both (AAV-17 requires direction agreement, not phase). A slow honest ramp reads as a mechanical detent (step, then rest), which strengthens "honest rests, the lie never rests"; a fast ramp (a decompression) crosses a quantum every step and reads as continuous. The quanta in needle terms (D.1, D.4): `p_o2` 5 dkPa over a 300 dkPa span is 16.7 pm, 1.7 px on DIAL_L and 1.25 px on DIAL_S; `P` 10 dkPa over 1100 is 9.1 pm; `T` 1000 mC over 150000 is 6.7 pm; `stock` 20 pm is 1 px at `travel_px` 50. `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` 40 exceeds every single-quantum step (the largest is `p_o2`, 16.7 pm), so one quantum crossing never fires a settle on any quantity; on the one `settle_eligible` quantity, `load` (quantum `LOAD_QUANTUM_PERMILLE` 20 permille = 16.0 pm, D.1), three quanta accumulated inside the jump window (3 x 16 = 48 pm, over the 40 pm threshold; two = 32 pm, under it) do, see (b); the same three `p_o2` quanta (17 + 17 + 16 = 50 pm) are drawn by the D.1 ramp, because `settle_eligible` is false for `p_o2` (D.4). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4: conforms to the per-quantity `settle_eligible` gate of D.4)* (b) **Rest, jump and settle: rest is defined in time.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text defined rest per Graph step here and per sample in D.4 and AC-IW-17, a definition under which the settle could never fire on `p_o2` or `stock`.)* An instrument is **at rest** iff no honest sample has arrived for `INSTR_REST_STEPS` consecutive Graph steps (3 steps = 300 ms) and no settle is active; IW-11, D.4, E-IW-8, AC-IW-17 and the REST state of S2 all use this one definition. The first honest sample after rest opens a **jump window** of `INSTR_SETTLE_WINDOW_STEPS` Graph steps (4 steps = 400 ms) and records `rest_pm`, the value the needle held at rest. A *jump*, on a `settle_eligible` quantity only (D.4; `load` at MVP) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, is any sample inside that window with |`target_pm` - `rest_pm`| >= `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` (the honest change accumulated since leaving rest, not the change of one step): a valve flick, a repair, an `apply_damage`, a breaker closing. The jump converts the in-flight ramp into a settle: the drawn value is the closed-form underdamped step response of D.4 as a pure function of `(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` and `present_time`, overshoot at most 5 % of the jump, settling to rest within 250-400 ms, then exactly still. A run that does not reach the threshold inside its window is a **sweep** (a continuing decompression crossing a quantum every step): it never settles until rest is re-entered, so a sustained ramp does not stutter. **The honest signature is therefore "step, then rest"**: every honest change is a detent-like step that ends at rest, and a real jump of at least 40 pm is a heavier damped ease; the overshoot shows as a 1-px tip flip only for jumps of 216 pm (DIAL_L) or 288 pm (DIAL_S) or more (D.4), and on the verified manifest actions only the `load` dial settles (D.4 reachability table). **Reversal dwell.** The LS-20 buckets have no hysteresis, so an honest value hovering on a quantum edge would flip the needle 1-2 px at up to 10 Hz with no stress descriptor, which reads as a tremor on a calm reading and teaches the lesson backwards. A sample that reverses the direction of the last accepted change by no more than one quantum is held as a candidate and accepted only after it has been the current sample for `INSTR_REVERSAL_DWELL_STEPS` Graph steps (4 = 400 ms); a candidate that equals the held value, or is superseded, is dropped. The needle, the card and the card numeral all use the accepted `target_pm`, so a 10 Hz dither across a quantum edge produces at most one move (AC-IW-110). (c) **State.** Exactly one `(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` triple per instrument plus the presentation-local scalars `prev_honest_pm` of (a) and `rest_pm`, the window start step and the dwell candidate (`target_pm`, `candidate_pm`, `t_candidate`) of (b), the triple discarded after `INSTR_SETTLE_MS`, neither ever persisted, never replicated, never read by any other *system*; the instrument's wall node and its card are two views of one instrument object and both draw from its single drawn value, which is what makes card parity (IW-26) hold. The triple, `prev_honest_pm` and the scalars of (b) are cleared by any non-HONEST frame (the tremor scalars are not: they follow IW-12) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* and snapped by `hard_start` (the Filter's term, PF-33, raised by a kernel restore or `force_stage`), restore, camera cut and cull (IW-5, IW-33). The HUD's suit-arc settle (HS-14, `HUD_SETTLE_MS` 300 `[PH]`, HUD-owned; renamed there from `SETTLE_MS` after the collision, CF-HS-20) is a peer: it may cite `settle_response` (D.4) instead of restating a second curve, and this GDD's constants carry the `INSTR_` prefix so the two names never collide. (d) **Re-basing (orchestrator ruling: the ui-programmer's re-base adopted over the ux-designer's per-frame retarget, which would make the drawn value jump).** While a settle is active, any further change of the honest displayed value re-bases the triple: `from_pm` := the value currently drawn, `to_pm` := the new displayed value, `t_jump` := now; velocity is discarded (a small kink, accepted). So one triple always suffices, nothing accumulates, and a continuous ramp steeper than `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` per step degrades into a first-order-like follower whose overshoot of each tiny delta is sub-pixel (no rubbery bounce). (e) Any `motion_mode` other than HONEST clears the settle triple, `prev_honest_pm` and the reduced-motion notch at once, in that frame, and bypasses settle entirely: a lie never borrows settle (PF-17). It does NOT clear an honest tremor already running: that fades through `tremor_weight_pm` over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (IW-12, D.5, PF-8, PF-17). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* Reduced motion: settle becomes a step (IW-27). (advisor ruling R10; K-2)
*Why.* ART 7.3 mandates a damped settle ("the ship changed; the instrument caught up"). PR-8's rationale (PIPE:198) rejected "a gauge's needle lag" as presentation-owned state because it threatened the truth channel; a gauge is module-body, not truth channel, and the closed form is a pure function of three scalars derived from values the player was already shown, with PF-11's "modulo presentation-local state" as precedent. This is the one bounded exemption from PR-8's rationale and is **carried as K-2 for the PIPE owner to acknowledge**, not silently overridden. The continuous path uses the one PR-8 rule-5 interpolator, so rule 5 itself is not violated.
*Edge notes.* **CONFLICT K-17 (resolved by checkpoint ruling C14; the Filter and Graph refreshes are routed).** PF-7 memoises an honest ref "per sanity run and invalidated by the notification that dirtied it", the honest `Perceived` carries no previous value, PF UI Requirements forbid caching a `Perceived`, and LS-20 fires dirty keys only on quantum crossings (`p_o2` 5 dkPa, `P` 10 dkPa, `T` 1000 mC, store 20 permille). So even a Filter-supplied previous value could buy at best a one-step ramp between quanta, and the honest needle's resolution is the LS-20 quantum (rule (a)). **Refresh landed in the Filter (PF UI Requirements, 2026-10-27; OQ-IW-1 closed)**: the no-cache sentence now reads "never cache a `Perceived` record; a presentation-local scalar derived from an honest displayed value and cleared on any non-HONEST frame, cull, cut and restore is not a cache". The earlier request for a Filter-supplied `displayed_prev_pm` is withdrawn. Option (B), the Filter refreshing the honest memo every Graph step for refs that have an on-screen instrument (about 18 refs at 10 Hz), would give a smooth ramp at a per-step cost and is carried as OQ-IW-18, not MVP. LSG:998 ("gauges read `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles") is still routed to the Graph as a refresh (R18 wins). A lie onset during an active settle clears the triple and the drawn needle snaps to `displayed_pm` by at most the settle's current deviation (a tremor in progress at that moment is not cleared; it fades, IW-12) (the lie already shows its gleam floor and sound from its first frame, PF-15; the first lie is on a fault-free subject at rest, SN-16); letting the tail decay as an additive offset is **not** adopted (it brushes R8 and PF-17; OQ-IW-6). When the mode returns to HONEST (CLEAR, PF-12) no jump is detected because the displayed value tracked the true value during the return; a RETURN is a glide to truth, not a jump.

**IW-12. Honest tremor: driven only by physical stress, started only when HONEST.**
*Rule.* A DIAL or LINEAR instrument whose `motion_mode` is HONEST **and** whose stress predicate holds draws tremor: an irregular positional offset of at most `TREMOR_AMP_PX` (+-1 art px, ART 7.3), at 6-10 Hz, around the displayed value, with no gleam, onset ramp `TREMOR_ONSET_MS`, ceasing with decay `TREMOR_DECAY_MS` when the predicate ends, and resting on a pixel. At zoom rung `k` 1 the amplitude is raised to keep at least `TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX` (2) screen px (D.5; a refinement of ART 7.3's +-1, OQ-IW-4). The **stress predicate** (MVP) is any of: (i) an active hazard-mode FailureDescriptor on the bound node, mode in {1 LEAK, 2 SHORT, 3 OVERHEAT, 4 FREEZE, 5 BREACH, 7 OVERLOAD} (LS-11), with `sev` >= `TREMOR_SEV_MIN` (1), read through `failures(filter)`; never mode 10 WORN, 6 STARVE, 8 SEVERED, 9 SCRAM or **27 PATCH_WEEP** (a patched subject's steady weep, LS-11 row 27: `hp_cap < HP_FULL` with no mode 1-9 live, no `intensity_pm`; it is a consequence-channel witness of the patch, not a stress) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and never a compartment band descriptor (ATMO_COLD / HOT / THIN / DECOMP 20-23, AIRFLOW 24, PUDDLE 25): a band is a state, not a stress (advisor final-review amendment to R9: `warn_elapsed` is > 0 for every sev-1 subject, LSG D.11, so it is not a tremor input); (ii) an active OVERLOAD (mode 7) descriptor on a CABLE of the bound loop component, through `failures(filter)` (LSG:127); (iii) an active `SEAL_STRAIN` descriptor on an OPENING of the bound compartment, or a `LEAK` or `BREACH` descriptor on a HULL_SEGMENT or SEAM bounding it (subjects found through `nodes_in(cid)` and `neighbors(cid)`; read through `failures(filter)`); the subject lists of (i)-(iii) are precomputed at section load and recomputed only on a topology dirty key (`T`, `SEC/<id>`), never per frame. (iv) **`stress_active(section_id)`, off by default** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the MVP predicate is (i)-(iii) only, and (iv) is read only if the knob `TREMOR_USE_SECTION_STRESS` is true (default **false**, registered in Tuning Knobs); (K-13 resolved: the Graph now publishes the pure query, LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27; section stress is `stress_pm` = `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` 2000 while `step_no < stress_until_step`, set by M17 STRESS for `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` 600) for an instrument in that section. **(iv) is provisional and off:** M17 STRESS has one caller, Attention, which this rule forbids as a tremor driver (a tremor driven by it would make an instrument show Attention, which the header and IW-28 forbid, AT-17), and AT C1 reads a needle moved by real STRESS damage as a consequence and not a tell; the creative-director's position is that (iv) as written is a pillar-level conflict, so it stays off until the Attention owner and the creative-director confirm the contrary reading (OQ-IW-38); with the knob false the predicate is (i)-(iii) and `stress_active` is not read by Instruments. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The predicate is refreshed once per Graph step (IW-5). Tremor is never driven by Attention, sanity, a timer or a lie. A fading tremor is the honest tremor already in progress, not a lie's. It is positional, not luminous (HR-13 exemption; shown on the card as well, suppressed under `reduced_motion`, D96) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The tremor is STARTED and its predicate is read only when `motion_mode` is HONEST (advisor ruling R9; AT-17, AT:1415 C1). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Perception Filter publishes `tremor_weight_pm` and BREATH, PF-8, PF-17)* **Onset of a lie: a running tremor fades, it does not stop.** Instruments read `tremor_weight_pm` (int 0..1000, the tenth `Perceived` field, PF-8; 1000 on every HONEST frame; read from the same single `perceived()` pull as `displayed_pm`, never computed or cached here). In the first non-HONEST frame the presenter latches `env_hold := env` of the last HONEST frame (0 if no tremor was running) and from then on (a) no new tremor starts and no onset ramp runs in any non-HONEST frame (the predicate is not read; a flag cannot be set in a non-HONEST frame), (b) env stays `env_hold` (no rise, no decay of its own; the fade is carried by `tremor_weight_pm` alone), (c) the drawn offset is the D.5 offset multiplied by `tremor_weight_pm / 1000`, which falls linearly from 1000 on the first ACTIVE frame to 0 over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (Filter-owned, := `WANDER_ONSET_S`, 1.0 s `[PLACEHOLDER]`) and stays 0 until CLEAR, and (d) the flag clears and `env_hold` is discarded when `tremor_weight_pm` reaches 0, on `hard_start`, cull, camera cut and restore (so a restore mid-fade shows no tremor: Instruments never start one), and at the first HONEST frame after the lie (CLEAR): the predicate is then re-read and, if stress still holds, a fresh `TREMOR_ONSET_MS` ramp starts from env 0; `env_hold` is never carried across CLEAR. The **settle triple and the reduced-motion notch are the opposite: they are cleared at once** in the first non-HONEST frame (IW-11 (e), IW-27); under `reduced_motion` the tremor is not drawn, so there is nothing to fade and only the immediate notch clearing applies. Why the fade is `tremor_weight_pm` and not the 600 ms `TREMOR_DECAY_MS`: the tremor fades out over exactly the window in which the Filter's wander fades in (`TREMOR_BLEND_S` := `WANDER_ONSET_S`), so the onset second is never still (PF-17, AC-PF-46 bounds the onset rest on this); letting the predicate go false at onset would decay the envelope in about 0.3 s and leave about 0.7 s of near-stillness, and a tremor that stops dead at lie onset is itself a tell.
**On the card (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D96 — the card shows the honest tremor, suppressed under `reduced_motion`; K-18 resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.** The card shows the same honest tremor as its wall gauge (parity, IW-26; the same fade at lie onset, from the same presenter state and the same `tremor_weight_pm`; the amplitude is +-`TREMOR_AMP_PX` HUD art px, never scaled by the card multiple). With `reduced_motion` on, the tremor is suppressed on the card exactly as on the wall gauge and the held stress notch pair of IW-27 and D.10 shows in its place (two Hull Grey squares on the Ground plate above the dial) while the predicate holds and the reading is HONEST, so the stress tell never depends on motion for a player who has asked for less of it. The earlier objection (HR-13 says "no HUD shake"; ART:984 flags tremor's positional-not-luminous status as unconfirmed) is answered by this suppression and by the card frame, plate and keycaps never moving; the former fallback (the held notch on the card in all modes) is retired unless the user declines this default. Further accessibility-specialist advice is welcome when Accessibility Settings is designed, but nothing here waits on it.
*Why.* P2: the honest tremor is the instrument's share of the 10-30 s tell and is a real consequence the player can trace. "A needle moved by STRESS damage is a consequence, not a tell Attention drives" (AT C1). Because a tremor is only ever started on an honest reading (a running one fades at a lie's onset, it is never begun or driven by the lie), "shake = real" is a rule the game never breaks. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*
*Edge notes.* A patched or WORN subject carries only mode 10 WORN (LS-11, LS-23), so it does not tremble; its `warn_elapsed` is > 0 (LSG D.11), which is why `warn_elapsed` is not a tremor input. `alarm_eligible` (`sev` >= 3, LS-13) is not a tremor input; tremor begins at the first physical stress, always before the alarm class (`W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10 is the Graph's). If the predicate flaps at Graph-step rate, tremor flaps with it (10 Hz worst case); `TREMOR_HOLD_S` (default 0) is the playtest remedy. Tremor's perceptibility at `k` 1 on the largest field is marginal (D.7); the design accepts it, since the tell is for a player standing at the instrument. **Instrument tremor is never the only tell (stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 6).** It is this system's share of the P2 10-30 s tell and P2 is carried by several channels: every stress source in predicates (i)-(iii) above must also have a sound tell or a world-witness tell owned by Adaptive Audio or Failure & Trail (strain creak, hiss, drip, spark or frost, per the consequence channel), so zooming out to `k` 1, or standing outside the light, never removes the warning. This is a cross-owner requirement checked by AC-IW-106 and routed to Adaptive Audio and Failure & Trail.

**IW-13. Motion-mode dispatch.**
*Rule.* The Filter's `motion_mode` (HONEST, GLIDE, TICK, STALE, BREATH, RETURN) is the only switch: *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*

| `motion_mode` | Needle / meniscus | Numeral (card) | Settle | Tremor | Stress notch (RM) | Drawn value from |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HONEST | `displayed_pm` through IW-11 and IW-12 | steps once per real change (throttled, IW-14) | yes | yes if predicate (`tremor_weight_pm` 1000) | yes if predicate | Instruments |
| GLIDE | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | continuous tick follows | no | no new tremor; a tremor running at onset fades by `tremor_weight_pm` (D.5) | no (cleared that frame) | the Filter's value; Instruments draw it |
| TICK | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | continuous tick, `T_tick` (PF-18) | no | same as GLIDE | no | same |
| STALE | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | held digits | no | same as GLIDE | no | same |
| RETURN | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory: the rate-limited follower to truth) | follows | no | same as GLIDE (`tremor_weight_pm` is 0 once its blend is over and stays 0 until CLEAR) | no | same |
| BREATH *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: PF-8, PF-15 table, PF L335, L554)* | none: the surface is a static pair (state glyph, lamp-housing glow, machine state) with no needle; `frame_override` (the other honest frame of the pair, IW-17) is drawn and held still for the whole lie | none | no | no (a tremor exists only on a DIAL or LINEAR needle, IW-12, so none can be running; `tremor_weight_pm` is ignored) | no | `frame_override` from the Filter; the gleam breathes between `floor_eff` and `AMP_MAX_PM` over 4 to 6 s, drawn from `leak_amplitude_pm` exactly as IW-16 already draws any amplitude (no new behaviour) |

An honest gauge never glides; a lie never settles and never starts a tremor (a tremor already running at onset fades through `tremor_weight_pm`, IW-12, D.5); the instrument never infers a lie, it only obeys the mode. (PF-7 edge note, PF-17; orchestrator ruling R8 of the Filter run) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*
*Why.* If Instruments could decide, the player could read the truth from which animation applies: a P4 oracle.
*Edge notes.* The card has the identical dispatch (IW-26). A numeral-only READOUT (`gauge_kind` READOUT, no needle) lying FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL arrives as STALE (not BREATH) with its gleam breathing through `leak_amplitude_pm` (PF L334, L789); BREATH is the record mode of static-pair refs only (`.glyph`, `.housing_glow`, `.machine_frame`). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* **TICK and STALE are modes of the card numeral only** (checkpoint ruling C2): a wall gauge carries no digit (IW-6), and a `lie_displayed_value` lie moves a FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL needle toward its zone and never holds it. No lying needle rests: whatever the numeral's mode, the needle draws the Filter's trajectory, which never rests (PF-17), so the wall gauge keeps its motion mode while the card is closed (PF-8, HR-5). The numeral's STALE hold is a card-visible mode of the same lie, not a second one; the gleam and the motion mode remain mandatory and only the sound is droppable (PF-8).

**IW-14. The numeral: honest ticking, the throttle, and who owns the scheduler.**
*Rule.* Numerals exist only on the card (IW-6). An honest numeral steps once per real change of `displayed_value` at the quantity's `lsb`, never tweens and never counts up; a transition is a digit-glyph substitution in tabular cells (fixed width, slashed zero) of only the cells whose glyph changed, and never inverts a plate (PF-18; HR-13 is then checkable per cell). Honest transitions are throttled to the same ceiling as lying ones: the card's numeral updates on the HUD's shared **hold grid** `HONEST_TICK_MS` (owner HUD & Suit Layer, HS-14, pinned 500 ms and ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions, D91 iii) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the 400-500 range is withdrawn, the HUD's window-feasibility check leaves 30 ticks as the only feasible grid, HS-47; PF-18's 334 is the bound without the beacon share and is not used here), at most `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 transitions per rolling second; no second constant is registered here. At each grid boundary the numeral shows the **then-current** step (it may skip steps, never queued, never faded; it never shows a value the room did not have). The card's honest numeral changes only on the HUD's shared `HONEST_TICK_MS` grid boundary and adds no luminance event of its own (HS-47); a boundary at which no card digit changes is not an event; when the HUD's grid-skip rule skips a boundary the card shows the then-latest step at the next one, so honest numeral lag is at most `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS`. A lying numeral is the Filter's: a continuous tick or a stale hold under the shared scheduler `T_tick` = max(`LIE_TICK_MS` 400, N_r x 334) (400 / 668 / 1002 / 1336 ms for N_r 1..4; the 334 ms stagger floor keeps any closed 1 s window at or under `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3) (PF-18, registry `lying_digit_tick_schedule`); Instruments only draw the received digits. Formatting is integer-only: the displayed value is `displayed_value` converted by the quantity table (IW-9) with no float formatting; a temperature that rounds to -0 shows "0"; a value beyond the span shows the clamped bound with no "<" mark (a "<" would be a second reading); the format never reveals more precision than `lsb`. **`lsb` visibility lint:** for a lie-eligible dial, `lsb` must be fine enough that the digit changes at least every `T_VIS_MAX_S` during a glide at the floor rate (otherwise a lying numeral looks stale and the tri-modal rule loses a mode on the card): `p_o2` is therefore shown in kPa with one decimal (`lsb` 1 dkPa), not in whole kPa (D.12). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
*Why.* ART 7.3 (honest numerals tick); HR-13 (no luminance change faster than 3 Hz); PF-18.
*Edge notes.* **CONFLICT K-16 (raised by the ux-designer):** locked fact 21 / ART 7.3 say an honest numeral ticks "one step per real change, never a tween", while HR-13 and `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 cap digit-glyph substitutions at 3 per second; a breach would exceed the cap if every step were shown. This GDD throttles and shows the then-current step, exactly as HUD & Suit Layer does for its own honest numerals (HS-14 amends the same locked rule, and its K8 row accepts the amendment); exempting honest ticks from the ceiling is rejected because a photosensitive player gains nothing from the distinction. Honest grid boundaries on the card are not counted in the Filter's `N_r` (which counts lying readouts only); the combined HUD budget (card numeral plus suit numerals plus lying readouts) is the HUD's arbiter HS-47, which itself records an open counting unit and an ASK to the Filter and the accessibility-specialist when lying digits at `N_r` 2 or more fill the ceiling *(OQ-IW-9: HS-47 states that the card's honest numeral shares the HUD's grid boundary and adds no event; the open counting unit is HUD CF-HS-10)*. The digit mechanism (glyph-cell substitution from a `ui_` atlas versus a text node) is -> ADR candidate; tabular numerals, slashed-zero shaping and integer-scale snapping of a vector font are `[UNV]` for the pinned build and ART 7.1 makes them asset-test requirements. The same honest-digit mechanism is offered as a reusable component to HUD & Suit Layer for the field-check reading (IW-35).

**IW-15. Zone bands are coded by pattern first, hue second.**
*Rule.* Every dial and linear instrument carries zone bands derived **at build time** from LS-7 band names (D.2), never typed as numbers in instrument data. A band has a pattern class: SOLID (normal-class bands: `NORMAL`, `COMFORT`), HATCHED (caution: `THIN`, `LOW`, `COOL`, `HOT`, `FROST`), NOTCHED (critical: `HYPOXIC`, `ANOXIC`, `DECOMP`, `VACUUM`, `SCORCH`, `FREEZING`, `DEEP_COLD`; overload for `load`); the three must be distinguishable from each other at 25 % scale in greyscale (the hue-removed test). Gauge faces carry no loop hue (identity is the fitting silhouette and, while running, the pip); Alarm Red is never a zone colour (a static red band on every dial would make red common and decorative, violating ART 4.1). A zone narrower than `ZONE_MIN_ARC_PX` (6 art px of arc, D.2) fails a build lint: the instrument must use a larger size class or merge bands in data. The needle position is geometry; the needle is **not** coloured by the Graph's hysteretic `band_*` fields (advisor ruling R11).
*Why.* Hue-removed readability (ART 4.7, HR-5 test); LS-7 is the single source of bands.
*Edge notes.* Because LS-7 bands carry hysteresis (`H_P` 5 dkPa, `H_T` 500 mC) while dial zones are static intervals, the needle can sit inside the NORMAL zone while the Graph's `band_o2` still reads THIN: the dial is a continuous reading and no consumer compares them. The exact authored patterns (hatched dashes, split-rail, notched teeth) at a 3-row DIAL_S band are the pixel mock's to confirm (OQ-IW-3).

300	**IW-16. The gleam is drawn here, on glass and edges only.**
301	*Rule.* Instruments draw the gleam from `Perceived.leak_amplitude_pm` and the Filter's phase: hue fringe `#B07BE6` (never the core `#8A3FD1`), at an **edge** only (glass edge, needle leading edge, housing edge), never a fill, peak channel at most `LEAK_MAX_CH` (:= `DECOY_MAX_CH` 0.85), produced at runtime by a material parameter or modulate and never baked into a sheet (reserved-hue scan, ART:1207). **World gauge:** on the instrument's own material by a per-instance parameter (zero added draws); *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **fallback if per-instance CanvasItem shader parameters are unavailable in 4.7.2 (`[UNV]`):** a child edge sprite per lying instrument, cut from the `_msk` edge slice, whose `modulate.a` carries the amplitude: no new ShaderMaterial (the LO-13 budget of five holds) and one extra draw per lying on-screen instrument (a pooled material per quantised amplitude is rejected because it would spend the material budget); the edge thickness requested is the effective art px of D.9 (`ceil(2/k)` clamped 1-2, so at least 2 screen px at every rung; inside the Filter's `[PLACEHOLDER]` `GLEAM_EDGE_PX` range 1-2, PF-16, OQ-IW-4). **Card (the answer to OQ-PF-11 / PF C-3 for the card):** Instruments draw the gleam on the card's glass and needle edge and the digit well's top and bottom edge, in HUD art px (1 HUD art px = `H` screen px, `H` >= 3, so HR-12's 2-screen-px stroke always holds), from the same amplitude and phase as the wall gauge. The card frame, bezel and rivets are an anchor and never carry violet (PF-18, SNV-8). Cut order if Filter spike S-1 fails: housing and glyph gleams first, **never** the needle or the card numeral well (PF-42's "never needle and readout") (advisor ruling R5).
302	*Why.* The Filter owns amplitude and phase but no layer-2 node; HUD & Suit Layer (designed in this run) supplies only the frame and the gleam helper; the card glass is Instruments' node.
303	*Edge notes.* **Hue risk (art-director finding).** A gleam multiplied by a coloured light leaves the violet band: `#B07BE6` under the beam core `#FFE2A8` shifts toward magenta (hue about 321 degrees, still inside 270-330), and under Chemlight `#86B896` it reads blue (about 244 degrees), darker. A lying gauge lit only by a glowstick would lose its hue mode. Requirement: the gleam is composited so its hue is not modulated by the light's colour (intensity gated by the host's lit factor, hue fixed) -> ADR candidate (shared with the Filter's spike S-1 and OQ-PF-6); the motion mode survives regardless and HR-5 needs only each mode sufficient, so this is a risk, not a break. Instance-parameter transport and batching are `[UNV]` HIGH risk.

305	**IW-17. The Module-Body Presenter.**
306	*Rule.* For each module sheet the Presenter selects one **honest** frame from the Graph state and, where tagged, from `perceived(MACHINE_FRAME | HOUSING_GLOW | STATE_GLYPH).frame_override`:
307	
308	| Graph input (`node(id)`) | Honest frame from the sheet | Notes |
309	|---|---|---|
310	| `state` 0 OK, `served_pm` > 0 | `running` | rotor / moving-medium region animates (pipe-side witnesses are Failure & Trail's and Lighting's; the *machine's own* medium is part of this frame) |
311	| `state` 0 OK, `served_pm` = 0 | `stopped` | idle, not failed |
312	| `state` 1 DEGRADED without a hazard mode (WORN) | `running` or `stopped` plus the wear overlay (IW-18) | no condition word, no bar |
313	| `state` 1 DEGRADED with a hazard mode (1-9) | `running` or `stopped` by `served_pm` exactly as state 0, plus the wear overlay; `cracked` only for housings and tanks whose live hazard is LEAK or BREACH; the lamp pair follows `served_pm` (lit while `served_pm` > 0) | the machine still functions at reduced `eff` (LS-10); no condition word, no bar |
314	| `state` 2 FAILED | `stopped` for pumps and rotors; `cracked` for housings and tanks | lamp pair `unlit` (no function, LS-10) |
315	| `state` 3 DESTROYED | `cracked` plus the dead frame | binding lost (IW-30) |
316	| `state` 4 SALVAGED, 5 ABSENT | module gone; no frame | |
317	
318	`frame_override` swaps to the *other honest frame of the same pair* (running/stopped, whole/cracked, lamp lit/unlit); the Filter never supplies a frame the sheet lacks: SPRITE_SWAP eligibility is `has_both_frames(def_id, pair)`, **a requested Item DB query** that implements SN AC-SN-152's eligibility (it exists in no GDD today), and both frames of every lie-capable `mach_*` sheet sit on one sheet page. The Presenter reads the Graph for *which honest frame*, never for a displayed value. The **state glyph** is the same function: an 8x8 chamfered-square lens mark on the module housing with two frames of different *shape* (run: a filled lens with a 2-px inner tick; stop: a hollow lens with a 2-px diagonal bar) so they survive the hue-removed and greyscale tests; it carries no loop hue, no flow mark and no fitting silhouette (ART 8.2: an 8x8 mark never identifies a loop), and a glyph lie swaps to the other honest glyph frame *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's 8x8 shape-coded lens adopted over the ux-designer's 16x16 hue-while-running glyph; a hue swap beside a possibly lying needle is an oracle and fact 14 reserves 16x16 for HUD glyphs)*. No other sprite of the same module may draw the honest state beside an override; a WORN patch plate is a separate TRUTH-graded sprite (a lie that cracks a whole machine over a patch plate is a content lint case for Derelict Authoring, `PATCH_OVER_OVERRIDE`). (advisor ruling R7; PF-45, SN:1346)
319	*Why.* A SPRITE_SWAP lie is only fair if both frames are ordinary state tokens the player has seen.
320	*Edge notes.* ART 7.2 / 8.9 line 12 ("icons never swap to express state") needs an exemption for reading surfaces whose lie *is* a frame choice (state glyph, machine frames): bible refresh BR-1, the art-director's. Direction of change: the frame follows the same Graph value the audio reads (IW-32). Stage-3 machine frames and the stage-2 lamp-housing pair are the cuttable tier (IW-34).

322	**IW-18. WORN and patched presentation.**
323	*Rule.* A WORN subject (DEGRADED, no hazard mode, `medium` NONE, `acoustic` NONE; LS-11) shows module-body wear: the wear overlay frame (scuffs, and a visible patch plate if patched) on the machine and on the instrument bound to it; the gauge shows the perceived reading of the module's output as usual. No word, bar, rating, colour grade or numeral says "worn" (BS-6, IA-39). A patched subject is permanently DEGRADED `sev` 1 (LS-10, D.4) and keeps its patch plate; the plate is driven by the node's patched state (`hp_cap < HP_FULL`; the Graph's PATCH_WEEP id 27 row uses the same condition and draws the weep on the consequence channel, which Instruments never touch) and not by the WORN descriptor *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Failure & Trail draws nothing for WORN (FT:232, :637). The wear overlay is corruptible only through the machine-frame swap at stage 3 (a false-fixed scrubber looks whole while its witness says otherwise); it is honest at stages 0-2. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP: the Module-Body Presenter owns the patch plate, so it gains the D39 bead axis that Interaction D.1b needs and that Failure & Trail cannot draw, FT-32 row 27 being one static POINT_FIXED mark with no length axis.)* **Patch-plate bead.** The patch plate carries a weld bead of 1, 2 or 3 segments (user-confirmed default D39, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20); registry `bead_segments`, owner Interaction D.1b): the Presenter selects one of three bead frames of the plate overlay by `bead_segments(h) = clamp(1 + floor(2 * (h - LEAK_HP) / (PATCH_CAP_BP - LEAK_HP)), 1, 3)` with h = the subject's true `hp` from the Graph (LS-19: `node_hp(id)`, or the `hp` field of `edge(id)` for an edge). At registry defaults (`LEAK_HP` 4000, `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000, span 2000): hp 4000-4999 gives 1, 5000-5999 gives 2, 6000 gives 3. h equals the banked hp at the end of the patch for the whole `PATCH_DECAY_S` 240 s hold, then falls with the wear (100 bp per 10 s: 5900 gives 2), so the bead shortens as the patch wears. The bead is the only thing that varies between the three frames: no numeral, word, colour change or overlay (BS-6, IA-39, AD-14). The hp read is made in the same per-step non-value read as the frame selection (IW-5), so the AC-IW-62 read count is unchanged and nothing is read per frame. Frames: three bead frames of the patch-plate overlay (`ovl_patch_<loop>_alb`), authored once per module sheet, inside the P0 "WORN overlay and patch plate" row. The plate and bead are drawn from the patched state (`hp_cap < HP_FULL`), stay drawn under a stage-3 swap (E-IW-38) and are removed by a FULL repair (`hp_cap` back to `HP_FULL`). The patched-not-cured tell on the consequence channel is the Graph's `27 PATCH_WEEP` weep, which this system never touches.
324	*Why.* Routed thread 5; BS-6 and IA-39: no condition surface.
325	*Edge notes.* Wear frames are authored once per module sheet, never per loose item (AD-BS-5 forbids a per-loose-item wear set as "the inspect card in disguise"). WORN is shown here on module-body surfaces only; the card shows no wear (IW-22). LS-11 (mode 10 WORN: "readable on the sprite, the gauge and the inspect card") and LSG:168 are read as: WORN reaches the card only through the module's reduced output reading; the card carries no wear frame, word or mark (advisor ruling R2).

327	**IW-19. The in-world alarm mark: TRUTH-graded, on the housing, alarm-eligible only.**
328	*Rule.* While the bound subject has an `alarm_eligible` failure descriptor (LS-13; severity >= 3; read through `failures(filter)`), an instrument housing that can carry it shows one Alarm Red `#E0102A` chamfered-square warning mark (ART:817 shape, ART 7.2 canonical size 16x16 art px, `ALARM_MARK_WORLD_PX` 16, "nothing smaller") on the **housing, not the face**. The world twin's exclamation stroke is **Void Steel**, not Paper White (Paper White is UI-only, fact 16, ART 4.6; the HUD twin keeps Paper White). **Where the mark may be drawn (stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 1, P4 cost rule; rewritten 2026-10-27 as a decision table).** The mark is drawn only on a housing that is physically at the alarm-eligible subject. That is a property of placement data (`mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node`, IW-8) and not of a tag: the decision table below lists every case. An instrument with `hops(mount_room, subject_room)` >= 1 (REMOTE) satisfies none of the yes rows, so the lethal remote FALSE_OK of Beat C is never put beside its own contradiction by a lit Alarm Red mark on the lying instrument's housing, and believing the mark still costs a walk to where the subject is (P4: checking costs time, risk or trust). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The mark itself stays TRUTH-graded and untagged; this rule decides only on which housings it is drawn, from authored placement data (`mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node` and the binding), never from a lie state. The mark lives on a DIAL_L housing meeting that test (in the 36 px horizontal bay beside the 60x46 housing), on machine and console panels and on the tank prop meeting it; **DIAL_S carries none** *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's narrowing adopted over the ux-designer's 4-row overlap of the DIAL_S arc; a 16x16 mark cannot sit on a 46x35 housing in a 48x48 cell; K-15 is therefore reframed from "overlap" to "which housings carry the mark", route art-director; the DIAL_S instrument's consequence-channel hiss, draught and sweep are its alarm)*. It is an **untagged node** (PF-4 default TRUTH), separate from every corruptible ref, so no HOUSING_GLOW or MACHINE_FRAME lie can add, move or suppress it; it is a witness and never itself a lying surface (SN L-A, SN:262). It never appears as the first warning (`alarm_eligible` is the only state in which an alarm-class presentation may play, and `W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10 guarantees a prior tell on endogenous transitions). `alarm_eligible` is a field of the `FailureDescriptor` (LS-14) that also requires the fairness gate to be open: Instruments **never re-derive it from `sev`**. The mark pulses in the beacon rhythm (2-3 s period, never faster than 3 Hz, HR-13; ART 7.3), holds solid under reduced motion, is non-emissive, casts no light and is lit-gated by the renderer like the housing. The needle and zones keep showing the perceived reading. The card does not carry the mark. **Decoupling rule (so the mark is never a free falsifier):** a zone's onset (an LS-7 band edge) and `alarm_eligible` (`sev` >= 3) are different quantities and do not coincide; **the absence of the mark never proves a needle in an alarm zone is lying** (the rule is one-directional: absence is never evidence; presence is the ship speaking and outranks the needle, E-IW-37), and a lying FALSE_FAIL needle in an alarm zone without a mark is not distinguishable from a true reading approaching alarm on that evidence alone (advisor ruling R14; K-8).
329	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **IW-19 decision table (housing, mount, binding, `hops`).** A mark also requires an `alarm_eligible` descriptor on the bound subject (above); the table decides only whether the housing may carry one.
330	
331	| Row | Housing and mount | Binding | `hops` | Mark? |
332	|---|---|---|---|---|
333	| (a) | machine or console panel (a module's own housing; no instrument needed) | `host_node` = the alarm-eligible node | 0 by construction | yes |
334	| (b) | LINEAR on a tank or reservoir prop | `host_node` = the tank's `stock` node, which carries the descriptor | 0 by construction | yes |
335	| (c) | DIAL_L, WALL_FACE | compartment ref with `mount_room` = `subject_room` | 0 | yes |
336	| (d) | DIAL_L, WALL_FACE | compartment ref with `mount_room` != `subject_room` | >= 1 (REMOTE) | **no** |
337	| (e) | DIAL_L, WALL_FACE | node ref or loop-component ref (a bus, a cable, a pump) | any | **no** (not on that node's own panel) |
338	| (f) | DIAL_L, MACHINE_PANEL | `host_node` = `subject_node` | 0 | yes (the panel's mark of row (a)) |
339	| (g) | DIAL_L, MACHINE_PANEL | `host_node` != `subject_node` | any | **no** |
340	| (h) | DIAL_S, GLYPH, FRAME, the card | any | any | **no** (no 16x16 bay; hiss, draught and sweep are its alarm) |
341	
342	**Count.** Of the 18 manifest instruments, 6 can carry the mark: 3 DIAL_L by row (c) (`inst_cryo_bay_p_o2`, `inst_cryo_bay_T`, `inst_b_reactor_T`) and 3 tank sight-glasses by row (b) (`inst_res_main_level`, `inst_home_fuel_level`, `inst_res_b_level`). The other 12 never do: 3 DIAL_L by rows (d) and (e) (`inst_engine_bus_load`, `inst_a_machine_T`, `inst_b_dock_p_o2`), 6 DIAL_S and 3 GLYPH by row (h). Each manifest instrument's row is in the IW-29 table. **P0 asset re-justification.** The 16x16 world mark stays one P0 sheet because its principal hosts are not instruments: the machine and console panels of every alarm-eligible node (rows (a) and (f)) and the tank props (row (b)) carry it, and the manifest's own dials add only 3 hosts. If the art-director rejects the second Alarm Red surface (BR-3) the fallback is unchanged: no mark.
343	
344	*Why.* P2 (the alarm class is never first) and P4 / SN L-A (a true alarm cannot be suppressed by a lie).
345	*Edge notes.* ART:375 / :400 / :463 grant "a failing instrument's warning mark"; ART:817 says the mark "lives on the critical strip" and "Alarm Red appears nowhere else on the UI": the bible is split against itself; the art-director's reading (ART 7.2's sentence is about the screen-space UI layers; a world mark on a physical housing is not UI) is adopted pending its refresh (BR-3). Fallback (b), if the art-director rejects a second Alarm Red surface: no mark (sweep and sound only), which changes nothing else here. The mark's exact absence on DIAL_S is confirmed against the pixel mock S-A1.

386	*Rule.* In the `inspect_card` context *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: entering the context sends `set_move_intent {NONE}` and clears the run latch but does not cancel a running channel (PC contexts note: the second-instrument check on the pipe being welded costs nothing); zoom stays reachable; `inspect`, `cancel` (X) and B close the card; the sim keeps ticking and the HUD critical strip stays live, so a breach during inspection is felt through the consequence channel. **Movement past the dead-zone closes the card and moves the avatar in the same frame; no move press is swallowed.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Two refinements that do not reverse D94: (1) **held-at-entry latch**: a direction already held (a key or a stick octant) at the moment the context is entered is latched and is not a fresh move; it neither closes the card nor moves the avatar until it returns to neutral or changes octant, so pressing `inspect` while running does not close the card on the next frame (the latch is the Controller's, requested, OQ-IW-44); (2) **card dead-zone margin for a gamepad stick**: while the card is open the stick's effective dead-zone is `MOVE_DEADZONE + CARD_PAD_DEADZONE_MARGIN` (a tunable, default 0.10 normalised `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 0-0.25, exposed to the accessibility settings), so stick drift or a tremor in the hand does not close the card unintentionally; a stick inside the enlarged dead-zone does nothing, as inside the plain one, and a deliberate push past it closes the card and moves in the same frame. A keyboard has no margin. The earlier rule zeroed and swallowed the first move press, which with lethal friendly fire and restart from the last autosave could kill a player by eating an input, and the UI frame must never betray the player. P3's stillness cost survives because the gauge must stay in the beam: a player who steps away loses `lit` anyway. A move also interrupts a running channel as any move does (PC-7). **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): D94 ratified.** The PC context matrix is amended (`move_*` in `inspect_card`: closes the card, then live) and the Controller's GDD carries the amendment; the buffer-and-replay fallback is retired (OQ-IW-17, AC-IW-39) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **Aim and cursor (K-14 closed 2026-10-27):** `set_aim` stays live so the chest lamp can hold the gauge lit, and the OS cursor is hidden and inert in `inspect_card` (PC-16, the PC context matrix, HS-52). The card is seat-local: never replicated, never visible to another seat, never a command; each seat's card reads `perceived(ref, its own PlayerId)`; a teammate's beam keeps `lit(ref)` true for my card (lit is world state) but my reach loss closes it. **Opening the card is not a falsification:** it is not a channel, lies identically to its gauge and so can never debunk; it calls no `record_falsification`; OQ-SN-12's INSPECT `check_kind` is reserved for any future *channelled* inspect verb (VS-A) (advisor ruling R13, R20).
387	*Why.* SN-16 / AD-C1: the card must never be a free falsifier; P4 needs a precision tool that is not a truth oracle. Answers the condition in AC-SN-111.
388	*Edge notes.* A teammate's friendly harm while the player stands still in the card context is the consequence channel's business: the player may close the card at any time at no cost, by `inspect`, `cancel` or simply by moving. Two cards cannot open per client (one seat per client).
389	
390	**IW-26. Card parity: the same instrument, not a second one.**
391	*Rule.* The card uses the **same** `PerceptionRef` as its wall gauge (there is no card ref and no card lie), reads the same `Perceived` through the same memo, shows the same drawn value (it reads the instrument's own settle triple and tremor state) (including a tremor fading through `tremor_weight_pm` at a lie's onset: the card and the wall draw the same offset in the same frame; opening the card mid-fade shows the fade in progress, never a new tremor) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*, the same motion mode, the same gleam parameters and the same HR-5 tri-modal tell, from stage 1. A lie that starts, ends or changes while the card is open appears on the card in the same frame as on the wall gauge, with no flash of the true value. Closing and reopening a card on an active lie shows the same `Perceived` and plays no new sound (the sound is the Filter's request on the ref, not on the card). Opening the card never replays a settle and never sweeps the needle in from zero. "Second instrument" in P4 is always a *different* gauge elsewhere, never the card. The card dial renders the same angle set as the wall needle (it must not be a more precise render of a lying value than the wall is of the same value). The card numeral is `displayed_value` of the **same** `.needle` ref's `Perceived` (checkpoint ruling C2): it is not a second lie target and carries no `lie_surface_id` of its own. In every non-HONEST mode the card needle draws `displayed_pm` verbatim plus any fading tremor offset (the Filter's trajectory, wander included, which never rests), while TICK (continuous tick) and STALE (held digits) govern the numeral only, so the card and the wall gauge never disagree about which motion mode is active (PF-9, PF-18, AC-PF-23; HR-14).
392	*Why.* Otherwise the card is either a free falsifier or a separate lie target.
393	*Edge notes.* The card has no module-frame surface, so if the wall shows a stage-3 `whole` frame while the module is `cracked`, the card shows only the reading and there is nothing for it to disagree with. Stress is the one honest-only difference of *form* that may arise (tremor versus the held notch under `reduced_motion`, K-18 resolved by D96); it is honest-only on both and never differs in a lie *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
394	
395	#### Group F. Boundaries, content floors and fallbacks
396	
397	**IW-27. Reduced motion and accessibility substitutes.**
398	*Rule.* With reduced motion (HR-8): honest settle becomes a **step** (drawn = `displayed_pm`); honest tremor is replaced by a **held stress notch pair** (each `max(NOTCH_PAIR_PX, ceil(NOTCH_MIN_SCREEN_PX / k))` art px, at least 4 screen px at every rung *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), shown while the IW-12 predicate holds **and** `motion_mode` is HONEST, and never on a lying reading (it would be an oracle): the notch pair is removed in the first non-HONEST frame, immediately and not faded (under `reduced_motion` no tremor is drawn, so `tremor_weight_pm` has nothing to blend; PF-8 keeps the immediate clearing of the notch and of the settle triple) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*; the alarm mark holds solid. Glide, wander and lying-tick scaling are the Filter's (PF-39: `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` 0.6, rate floor not below 0.3 deg/s, wander never scaled, lying tick never below `LIE_TICK_MS`) and are not restated. The notch is two Void Steel nicks cut into the world bezel's top edge about 4 px either side of centre, and, on the card, two Hull Grey squares on the Ground plate above the dial *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's placement adopted; R19 said "on the bezel", but HR-2 forbids Hull Grey on a bezel fill, so the card's notch sits on the Ground side of the dial rim)*. No setting removes a leak mode, hides the gleam or the card numeral, or adds an Attention or sanity surface. Instrument labels and the card obey the 21/15 text tier and UI scale `H`; the instrument face is a bitmap font at integer `H` only (advisor ruling R19). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Reduce flashing defaults ON at first launch** (user ruling, D79): the card's honest numeral already rides the shared hold grid (D.3) and adds no flash surface that the default would need to suppress; under the HUD's stricter arbiter for reduce flashing (HS-47) a grid boundary may be skipped and the card shows the then-latest step at the next one, which the lag bound of `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS` already covers. Card tremor is suppressed under `reduced_motion` (IW-12, D96).
399	*Why.* HR-8: the backbone of the lie (never-rest, continuous tick) survives; tremor is the one signature that needs a static substitute.
400	*Edge notes.* Accessibility Settings (Alpha) depends on this GDD (IDX:209): its reduced-motion toggle reads the Filter's published scalars (`reduced_motion_glide_pm`, `breath_depth_pm`, `lie_tick_min_ms`) and this rule's substitute *(provisional — Accessibility Settings undesigned)*. The screen-reader text for a card (Alpha) is built from `Perceived.displayed_value` only, never `true_value`; the pinned engine's accessibility live-region maturity is `[UNV]`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Tell survival for a deaf, colour-blind player.** With the sound removed and the hue removed, a lie keeps the never-rest motion mode on the needle, the continuous tick on the card numeral and the gleam as a **luminance** fringe; the claim of at least two tells therefore holds only if the fringe `#B07BE6` keeps at least `GLEAM_LUM_CONTRAST_MIN` 3:1 (the WCAG non-text ratio, `[PLACEHOLDER]`) against the glass it rides in greyscale, measured at S-A1 and tested by AC-IW-120. **Tell-survival rule** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: for every combination of reduced motion (scale 0.6), captions on or off, greyscale or a colour-vision filter, and sound off, at least two of the three tells survive on every lying instrument: the never-resting needle (the wander is never scaled, PF-39), the luminance gleam (above `GLEAM_LUM_CONTRAST_MIN`) and the sound (not counted when sound is off or unheard). The numeral tick is a mode of the motion tell and is not counted as a separate tell. Where reduced motion lengthens a digit hold, D.12 accepts it explicitly (`T_VIS_MAX_RM_S`). Tested by AC-IW-125; the caption tier is recorded in `design/accessibility-requirements.md` once that file exists (OQ-IW-42). Captions for lie sounds (Alpha) are a gate dependency of the accessibility tier and not an Instruments feature. `design/accessibility-requirements.md` does not exist; `/ux-design accessibility` sets the tier (OQ-IW-42).
401	
402	**IW-28. What Instruments never do (scope guard).**
403	*Rule.* No schematic, overlay, minimap, ship-status, loop-summary or "lit schematic console" screen, ever; **rejected: lit schematic console** (answers CT:63, CT-1 at CT:223, CT:537 and CT:685 C4; LSG:51 anti-pillar 3). No numerals on a world gauge; no text on an in-world gauge; no closed ring or progress ring (curves are reserved for dial arcs and needles, ART 3.4); no condition word, bar, rating or loot value; no weld-preview number or seam readout (`surge[]` is never printed, LSG:170); no sanity meter, lie counter, "spotted" statistic, stage name or Attention, threat-level, proximity or direction indicator on any instrument (nothing Attention publishes feeds a needle); no instrument shows a horror, a threat level, a proximity or a direction (Pillar 3; HE Interactions downstream); a needle moves only when the ship's loop moves, the tell never moves one, and no instrument displays or sonifies the Attention level (AA UI Requirements; AT-17); no reading of a crewmate or a horror; no Alarm Red word; no violet or flesh pixel in an authored sheet; no pod dash; no new sim state, hook, mutator or block. A lint over the scene asserts that no node outside an instrument or the card renders Graph state at a distance (advisor ruling R16; PF-38; HE:377).
404	*Why.* Anti-pillars (no combat, no PvP, no authored story, no win state) and P1.
405	
406	**IW-29. The MVP manifest is a content floor plus an indicative list.**
