**IW-20. Sight-glass split, and linear instruments.**
*Rule.* Flow patterns on pipes (chevrons, dash-pulse, banding, static on dead branches) and the motion of a pipe's moving medium are world-state witnesses (TRUTH_PX, PF-5 rows 17a and 17b), drawn by Lighting and Failure & Trail, never by this GDD. The **fill-level reading of a tank sight-glass** (the home fuel tank, WM-20; the coolant reservoirs `res_main` and `res_b`; the O2 tank at the top-up port, SE VA-23) is a corruptible module-body reading drawn here as a LINEAR instrument whose level is the Graph `stock` (after M16 mutations). A machine's own moving medium belongs to its machine frame (IW-17) and is corruptible only by stage-3 SPRITE_SWAP. A LINEAR instrument is a vertical glass tube (housing about 12x62 on the 48x96 tank prop, clear of the pipe band because the tank is a prop) with a baked fluid column in the stored medium's palette hex (stock, not flow: lit-only and not emissive, so a dead loop's tank still shows its fuel), a 6x2 meniscus bead (6 wide, 2 tall, IW-7 arithmetic) that is the element that settles, trembles or glides, scale ticks at 0/25/50/75/100 % (no numerals), and a zone strip in the same three patterns; `travel_px` 50 `[PLACEHOLDER]` so that 1 art px = 20 permille = the store dirty-key quantum (LS-20), one size at MVP *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's 50 px single size over the ux-designer's 24/16 two sizes; a longer travel keeps a lie's visible departure above 4 px and the glide rate above the never-rest rationale)*. The Filter's angle maths has no linear branch; the linear glide band is stated in pixels (D.11; request to the Filter, K-5): a visible departure `D_VIS_MIN_PX` and a rate floor `LINEAR_GLIDE_RATE_MIN_PXS` (0.5 px/s, the same tip-speed rationale as PF-17). A LINEAR instrument below a minimum travel is ineligible for travel lies (`TRAVEL_MIN_PX`, `[PLACEHOLDER]` 40; it keeps gleam and numeral modes). (advisor ruling R8)
*Why.* LS-22 Fuel row ("sight-glass module-body (corruptible)") reconciled with ART 2.3 and 3.5 ("fluid in the pipe proves the pipe"). The puddle, the drip and the pipe's flow pattern are the witnesses for the fuel tank; they share no node with the glass (FT:314).
*Edge notes.* The fuel loop's colour-blind backup (ART 4.7 Power vs Fuel) is the fill-level glass itself, so a lying home-tank sight-glass corrupts a backup channel on purpose; the pipe's flow pattern and the puddle remain the TRUTH backups. This is pillar-legal, but a colour-blind player then loses one more channel of truth than other players do, so P4's "at least one channel of truth" must hold per player and not on average: for each lie-eligible LINEAR instrument a hue-independent TRUTH witness (the pipe flow pattern or the puddle) must lie within `WITNESS_HOPS_MAX` (stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 5; AC-IW-105; routed to the accessibility-specialist next to OQ-IW-13). The fluid column is a baked palette hex in the `_alb` sheet, a deliberate deviation from ART 8.3 ("baking hue into albedo breaks the dead-loop rule") because it is stock not flow; the running-emission path stays on `_msk`. The pod has no dash at MVP, so no pod sight-glass exists (WM AB-2, K-10).

#### Group E. The inspect view

**IW-21. Targeting, permission and the prompt.**
*Rule.* An instrument is an OBJECT subject of IA-2 class `INSTRUMENT`, registered through Interaction's `sync_section` from Layout's `subject_anchors(section_id)` (IA-37), counted toward `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` and `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` by name (D.8). Focus is the standard aim-weighted proximity among in-reach, in-arc, **lit** interactables (PC-6; `REACH_PX` 72, half-angle 70 degrees, `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` 0.10). The prompt is Interaction's and HUD's standard lit-only plate: the keybind plus a state-neutral verb (`verb_inspect`, "R . Inspect"; RT on gamepad; the key is Interaction's and IA-38 and AC-IA-112 carry it since the 2026-10-27 consistency pass), drawn after `PROMPT_SHOW_DEBOUNCE_TICKS` 13 (HUD-owned; IA:892) and hidden immediately on unlit. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **`inspect` acts on the primary focus when that is an INSTRUMENT, and otherwise on the secondary INSTRUMENT slot**: the best lit INSTRUMENT in reach and arc by the same aim-weighted score (its own sticky margin), chosen independently of the primary focus. This is the arbitration for a MACHINE_PANEL gauge: with one sticky focus either the gauge took focus from the repair or valve prompt, or the gauge could not be inspected and `interact` on it gave no feedback. Now a valve or repair target holds the primary focus and keeps `interact`; the gauge on the same panel is inspected from the secondary slot; when both exist the plate lists both verbs (the primary verb, then `verb_inspect`) and each button acts on its own target. `interact` on an instrument still does nothing (no verb). No cycle control is added. This is a requested amendment to PC-6 and IA-2 (one primary focus plus one inspect-only secondary slot) and is provisional until the Controller and Interaction reply (OQ-IW-39, AC-IW-113). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Secondary-focus affordance:** when the secondary slot is occupied the `verb_inspect` row of the plate is drawn **anchored beside the secondary gauge** (the standard lit-only plate grammar at the gauge's `world_to_hud(anchor_px)`), and the primary verb's row stays on the primary target, so the player sees which gauge `inspect` will read; if the plates would overlap the inspect row takes the side away from the primary row. The marker is a plate anchor and a keycap, never a hue or a state word (pattern, not colour: the same keycap shape on every plate). **Which rule is in force until OQ-IW-39 closes: the fallback.** Until the Controller and Interaction accept the secondary slot, the placement rule governs: no INSTRUMENT shares a MACHINE_PANEL with an interactable verb target, enforced by the lint `PANEL_GAUGE_VERB_CONFLICT` (a build ERROR, owned by Derelict Authoring's lint set, IW-31); the amendment, if accepted, relaxes the lint to a warning. Under the fallback a battery dial (`inst_battery_stock`, `inst_b_a1_stock`), which the manifest places on its panel beside the breaker verb, would trip the lint, so until the amendment is accepted those two dials are placed `WALL_FACE` on the wall beside the panel and not on it; if the amendment is declined that placement stays and nothing becomes uninspectable. **Input versus prompt.** `PROMPT_SHOW_DEBOUNCE_TICKS` 13 and `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` 20 delay **drawing the plate only**; `inspect` is accepted on any frame in which the target holds focus and `lit(ref)`, including the frames before the plate is drawn and the frames straight after a close (IA: "the verb works as soon as it is focused"). The debounce clock starts at the tick the target became the stable focus and restarts when the plate hides; it never gates a press. **`inspect` is a permission rule only:** a presentation-only context switch (`inspect_card`), not a simulation command, permitted only on a lit instrument; no command type of that name exists. Gamepad proximity focus plus this one contextual action satisfies HR-14 (advisor ruling R23, D12; IA-38, AC-IA-112). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
*Why.* One focus model (PC-6); a cycle control or "nearest lit instrument regardless of focus" would add input or break the one-focus model.
*Edge notes.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: IA-38's own dormant sentence and the other stale assumptions listed here were refreshed by their owners in the 2026-10-27 consistency pass.)* If the card is cut, `inspect` stays bound and dormant (IA-38) and stage-1 reach loses the card surface; nothing else changes (advisor ruling R1; K-12, which lists the stale "dormant" assumptions owed a refresh: BS:183, BS:332, PC:210 row 10, PC OQ 4, IA OQ 16, IA-38's "If the card does not ship" sentence). This GDD answers PC OQ 4 and IA OQ 16: **the card ships live at MVP**, because it is the only numeric precision path (ART 3.1 forbids numerals on world gauges), HR-14 needs the mirror card, and SN-16 reach stage 1, PF-18, AC-PF-23 and AC-SN-122 are all written against a card that lies from stage 1.

**IW-22. Card content: label, one numeral with its unit, the same dial. No verdict.**
*Rule.* The card carries exactly: (1) the instrument's label = `name_key` (the reading's name, e.g. the quantity on a specific fitting; caps, Hull Grey on Ground, 5 art px cap); (2) the same needle or meniscus and zone bands as the wall instrument, at HUD art px, drawn at an integer multiple `CARD_MAG` of HUD art px (**fixed at 1**, range 1-2; checkpoint ruling C7: the 72x72 plate at `H` 6, the maximum on 1080p, is 432 px, 40 % of the height, and at `CARD_MAG` 2 the plate would break `CARD_MAX_FRAC_H` 0.5 at maximum `H`, so 2 cannot be the default; a conditional `CARD_MAG` 2 where it fits is a Vertical Slice revisit, OQ-IW-15); (3) one numeral with its unit in the bitmap instrument face (tabular numerals, slashed zero), Paper White `#DDE4EA`, 7 art px cap (21 screen px at `H` 3). Never OK / FAILED / DEGRADED / WORN or any condition word, rating or bar; no reason string; no true value beside a lying one; no lie count, stage name, verdict or sanity-correlated icon (PF-38); no module-state frame and no wear; no alarm mark (IW-19); no loop glyph (the art-director proposed a 16x16 Graphite loop glyph; R2's list is closed, so it is not carried, OQ-IW-16). All text goes through `tr()` with StringName keys (advisor ruling R2; K-3). **Division with HUD & Suit Layer** (HS-57, HS-48): HUD supplies the card's *frame register*: the chamfered bezel nine-slice, the single `Theme`, the tabular-numeral label and the gleam-on-glass helper; this GDD owns the card's *contents* (label, dial, numeral, glass), its context and its parity with the wall gauge. The frame is bit-identical with the Filter on or off and never gleams (HS-3); the gleam is applied to the card's reading glass through the HUD's helper, driven by the amplitude and phase the Filter supplies (IW-16).
*Why.* BS-6 ("no ... inspect-card condition"), IA-39 (no reason string), FT-4 and SN L-A: a state word is an oracle with no world analogue; the lie can only be a number and a needle. IDB:1074's "may name the module and its state in words" is answered **no** for state and **yes** only for the instrument label (routed to Item DB as a refresh).
*Edge notes.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Why open the card: three authored decisions the zone band cannot answer.** The card ships live at MVP, so it needs a stated use beyond "precision"; each row ties a decision to an authored instrument and to a number in this GDD.

| Decision | Instrument and authored fact | Why the band or the needle is not enough | What the card adds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Is the second opinion agreeing, or has a lie started? | the two `p_o2` dials, `inst_cryo_bay_p_o2` and `inst_engine_room_p_o2` (L-2I partners) | A floor-rate glide moves `p_o2` 1.5 dkPa/s (PF D.2 at 24 px); one tip pixel is 3.0 dkPa, so the needle departs by a pixel after about 2.0 s and the zone band not at all | The lying numeral ticks in single `lsb` steps (1 dkPa), so its digit has changed within about 0.7 s (D.12 `T_digit`), 1.3 s sooner than the needle shows a pixel; the honest partner numeral moves only in the Graph's 5 dkPa quanta (LS-20), so "the digit keeps moving while the partner holds" is the readable tell, and the numeral is no more precise than the quantum *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* |
| Is the reactor room still below the heat damage onset? | `inst_b_reactor_T` in the HOT band (42 C authored, DA); `HEAT_DMG_ONSET_MC` 45000 sits inside the HOT zone (40 .. 70 C) and the dial draws no tick there | The band says HOT for the whole 30 K; the needle's 2 px between 42 C and 45 C is not a threshold the player can see | A whole-degree numeral to compare with the onset the suit taught (the Graph's `T` quantum is 1000 mC, so the numeral resolves exactly the degree and no finer) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
| How much fuel is left against the hop? | `inst_home_fuel_level` (percent, `lsb` 10 permille) against `HOP_FUEL_ML` (WM-20, a placeholder) | The sight-glass resolves 20 permille per pixel and carries no mark for the cost of a hop | A numeral formatted in whole percent to decide whether to refuel before committing the pod; the honest value moves in 20 permille (2 %) store quanta (LS-20), so the numeral is good to 2 %, not 1 % *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |

The cost of opening is **time and keeping the gauge in the beam**; opening the card adds no Attention stimulus (Attention has no `inspect` class and the beam's light term accrues whether or not the card is open; confirmation requested, OQ-IW-40). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The card is therefore essentially free beyond what reading the gauge already costs, and the predicted equilibrium is that a player opens it often; that is accepted (D94 stands, and card parity makes it harmless). The exposure in Beat A comes from the dark room and from standing lit, not from the card. If the user wants the card to carry a real cost, the option is an Attention stationary-in-beam term, listed as an explicit option for the Attention owner in OQ-IW-40; this GDD does not add one.

"Magnified" (ART:747) means the same ref, the same drawn value and the same leak at HUD scale `H` with a label and a numeral, not a mixel-scaled sprite: at the default view (1080p, `k` 3, `H` 3) the card dial has the same screen size as the wall dial (the ui-programmer's C-UI-2); the card's value is zoom-independence (3.0x the world dial at `k` 1, 6.0x at 2160p `k` 1), an opaque Ground plate, the label and the numeral (D.7). `CARD_MAG` is 1 at MVP; a conditional `CARD_MAG` 2 where the plate fits is a Vertical Slice revisit (OQ-IW-15), not an MVP decision.

**IW-23. Card placement.**
*Rule.* The card is one opaque Ground plate (HR-2) at HUD scale `H_card` (D.6), at plate size 72x72 HUD art px `[PLACEHOLDER]` at `CARD_MAG` 1 (label row, dial block, numeral row, margins), snapped to the HUD art-px grid, anchored beside its instrument through `world_to_hud(anchor_px)` (the unjolted pose, quantised to the HUD grid; PIPE C11) and edge-clamped inside the 5 % safe margin like prompt plates. The **side** is chosen at open by trying right, left, above, below the instrument's screen footprint; the first candidate that (a) fits the safe area, (b) does not overlap the instrument's footprint, (c) does not cover the **chest-point keep-out** (a disc around the per-facing chest point, `CARD_KEEPOUT_CHEST_R`) and (d) does not cross the **beam corridor** (a capsule from the chest point to the instrument anchor, half-width `CARD_KEEPOUT_BEAM_HALFW`) and (e) does not cover a **teammate's figure** (a disc of `CARD_KEEPOUT_CHEST_R` around each other seat's chest point), a **lit interactable in reach** (its footprint) or the instrument's **witness anchor** (`witness_anchor_px`, a disc of `CARD_KEEPOUT_WITNESS_R`, so the plate cannot hide the drip, frost or crewmate that is the honest second reading) wins and is **latched**. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Every candidate is clamped to the safe rect and slid along its free axis on the HUD grid **before** it is tested, so the rectangle that is tested is the rectangle that would be drawn. If none qualifies, (a) and (b) stay hard and the soft constraints are relaxed in a fixed order: first `H_card` is stepped down one step at a time to `HUD_MIN_SCALE` and every candidate is tried again; only if no clean candidate exists at any `H_card` is a soft overlap accepted, choosing the candidate with the fewest violations in the order (c) chest disc, (e) teammate, interactable and witness, (d) beam corridor, then the least overlap area, then the larger `H_card`. The earlier fallback, "farthest from the chest point, clamped", could clamp the plate over the instrument it magnifies (reachable at 720p, `H` 6, `k` 4) and is retired. While the camera is stable the plate does not move; under camera drift (look-ahead continues while aim is live) its position is re-projected from `world_to_hud(anchor_px)` each frame on the grid so it stays attached to its instrument, and the side is re-chosen only on a cut (zoom, window resize, camera cut) or when the latched rect becomes invalid; a re-choice is a cut, never a slide. The plate never covers the instrument it magnifies (a hard rule under every fallback), the player's figure or the beam cone's origin (the beam stays the brightest thing, ART 3.5; avoided by (c), (d) and (e) whenever a clean candidate exists, D.6 reachability) (advisor ruling R3).
*(orchestrator ruling: R3's "held while the camera is stable and re-projected on a cut" is read as "does not move while nothing moves, follows its anchor under drift, side changes only on a cut". Read literally as a fixed screen position it would detach the card from its instrument by up to the look-ahead distance, the ui-programmer's C-UI-4; no Pipeline change is needed. The ux-designer's `CARD_REANCHOR_PX` drift threshold is retired in favour of per-frame follow.)*

No HUD element shakes under camera jolt (HR-13); `world_to_hud` is the unjolted pose. The world is never dimmed behind the card (ART 7.4).

**IW-24. Card lifecycle: immediate close, no dwell, real time.**
*Rule.* The card opens on `inspect` while the target (the primary focus or the secondary INSTRUMENT slot, IW-21) is lit and its ref is resolvable; there is no re-open debounce and no cooldown *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. It appears as a cut on the next render frame: no scale-in, fade, slide or pop (HR-13 forbids HUD scale change). It closes immediately, in the same render frame, on: `lit(ref)` false; `cancel` or B; a second `inspect`; kernel restore or `hard_start`; the instrument's binding lost (DESTROYED, SALVAGED, ABSENT or unresolvable); the instrument leaving reach; a section transit; **movement intent past the dead-zone (the card closes and the avatar moves in the same frame, IW-25)**; **any context change other than back to `gameplay`** (pause or `chart_table`, `chat`) and any `loco_state` change to `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `DEAD` or `IN_POD` (PC contexts note), each in the same render frame and **without re-opening** when the context returns. Re-open needs a new press and nothing else: only the plate's redraw obeys `PROMPT_SHOW_DEBOUNCE_TICKS` 13 (HUD-owned; IA:892, IA:1085; cited by name, no second value is registered), and a press is never dropped for it (IW-21). The real `cancel` key is X (B on a pad). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Light-loss unlatch cue:** a close whose cause is `lit(ref)` false (the beam drifted off) is the only close that is not the player's own act, so it plays a distinct, lighter **unlatch** cue (UI bus, `UI_INSTRUMENT_CARD_UNLATCH` requested from Audio, which owns naming and assets, provisional) on the same render frame, with no fade and no visual transition beyond the cut; no other close cause plays it. On the first light-loss close per profile, when `lit(ref)` next rises the `verb_inspect` plate is shown without the `PROMPT_SHOW_DEBOUNCE_TICKS` wait (once), using the existing keycap and no new text, so a reader can tell the rule ("it closes when the light leaves") from a bug. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The card is **not** a pause: the sim keeps ticking, the card runs in real time on `present_time`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* **Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling G2 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): pause closes the card, the creative-director's stated lean (P3: precision is a transient act that costs standing lit, not a state you bank).** Pause is a context change (`chart_table`), so it closes the card in the same render frame like any other; the needle then freezes with `present_time`. On resume the needle is bit-identical, the card stays closed, its plate does not animate back in, and a new `inspect` press is needed. A direction held through the pause neither re-opens the card nor is consumed by it (the card is already closed at the pause; held-input handling after a resume is the Controller's, OQ-IW-44). The IA-6 exemption "the inspect card of an already-lit instrument" means only that opening is not re-validated by `act_gate` as a command; it never permits a card on an unlit instrument (advisor ruling R4; EM-22). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
*Why.* EM-22: keeping `lit` true after the light went "would be a window where the sim says lit and the world is dark, a P1 lie"; P3: precision costs staying lit.
*Edge notes.* `lit(ref)` is read each render frame, so a card closes at most one tick after the light goes. At a pool edge the card closes once on the first false and stays closed: no strobe (HR-13). If the focus moves to another instrument while the card is open, the card stays on its latched ref; there is no navigation between instruments at MVP. A card opens only from the `gameplay` context on a press, never because `lit` turned on while the player was in `chart_table` or `chat`. A press whose ref has no instrument record is consumed silently with a diagnostic (no error text, no sound).

**IW-25. Card input, co-op and falsification.**
*Rule.* In the `inspect_card` context *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: entering the context sends `set_move_intent {NONE}` and clears the run latch but does not cancel a running channel (PC contexts note: the second-instrument check on the pipe being welded costs nothing); zoom stays reachable; `inspect`, `cancel` (X) and B close the card; the sim keeps ticking and the HUD critical strip stays live, so a breach during inspection is felt through the consequence channel. **Movement past the dead-zone closes the card and moves the avatar in the same frame; no move press is swallowed.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Two refinements that do not reverse D94: (1) **held-at-entry latch**: a direction already held (a key or a stick octant) at the moment the context is entered is latched and is not a fresh move; it neither closes the card nor moves the avatar until it returns to neutral or changes octant, so pressing `inspect` while running does not close the card on the next frame (the latch is the Controller's, requested, OQ-IW-44); (2) **card dead-zone margin for a gamepad stick**: while the card is open the stick's effective dead-zone is `MOVE_DEADZONE + CARD_PAD_DEADZONE_MARGIN` (a tunable, default 0.10 normalised `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 0-0.25, exposed to the accessibility settings), so stick drift or a tremor in the hand does not close the card unintentionally; a stick inside the enlarged dead-zone does nothing, as inside the plain one, and a deliberate push past it closes the card and moves in the same frame. A keyboard has no margin. The earlier rule zeroed and swallowed the first move press, which with lethal friendly fire and restart from the last autosave could kill a player by eating an input, and the UI frame must never betray the player. P3's stillness cost survives because the gauge must stay in the beam: a player who steps away loses `lit` anyway. A move also interrupts a running channel as any move does (PC-7). **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): D94 ratified.** The PC context matrix is amended (`move_*` in `inspect_card`: closes the card, then live) and the Controller's GDD carries the amendment; the buffer-and-replay fallback is retired (OQ-IW-17, AC-IW-39) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **Aim and cursor (K-14 closed 2026-10-27):** `set_aim` stays live so the chest lamp can hold the gauge lit, and the OS cursor is hidden and inert in `inspect_card` (PC-16, the PC context matrix, HS-52). The card is seat-local: never replicated, never visible to another seat, never a command; each seat's card reads `perceived(ref, its own PlayerId)`; a teammate's beam keeps `lit(ref)` true for my card (lit is world state) but my reach loss closes it. **Opening the card is not a falsification:** it is not a channel, lies identically to its gauge and so can never debunk; it calls no `record_falsification`; OQ-SN-12's INSPECT `check_kind` is reserved for any future *channelled* inspect verb (VS-A) (advisor ruling R13, R20).
*Why.* SN-16 / AD-C1: the card must never be a free falsifier; P4 needs a precision tool that is not a truth oracle. Answers the condition in AC-SN-111.
*Edge notes.* A teammate's friendly harm while the player stands still in the card context is the consequence channel's business: the player may close the card at any time at no cost, by `inspect`, `cancel` or simply by moving. Two cards cannot open per client (one seat per client).

**IW-26. Card parity: the same instrument, not a second one.**
*Rule.* The card uses the **same** `PerceptionRef` as its wall gauge (there is no card ref and no card lie), reads the same `Perceived` through the same memo, shows the same drawn value (it reads the instrument's own settle triple and tremor state) (including a tremor fading through `tremor_weight_pm` at a lie's onset: the card and the wall draw the same offset in the same frame; opening the card mid-fade shows the fade in progress, never a new tremor) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*, the same motion mode, the same gleam parameters and the same HR-5 tri-modal tell, from stage 1. A lie that starts, ends or changes while the card is open appears on the card in the same frame as on the wall gauge, with no flash of the true value. Closing and reopening a card on an active lie shows the same `Perceived` and plays no new sound (the sound is the Filter's request on the ref, not on the card). Opening the card never replays a settle and never sweeps the needle in from zero. "Second instrument" in P4 is always a *different* gauge elsewhere, never the card. The card dial renders the same angle set as the wall needle (it must not be a more precise render of a lying value than the wall is of the same value). The card numeral is `displayed_value` of the **same** `.needle` ref's `Perceived` (checkpoint ruling C2): it is not a second lie target and carries no `lie_surface_id` of its own. In every non-HONEST mode the card needle draws `displayed_pm` verbatim plus any fading tremor offset (the Filter's trajectory, wander included, which never rests), while TICK (continuous tick) and STALE (held digits) govern the numeral only, so the card and the wall gauge never disagree about which motion mode is active (PF-9, PF-18, AC-PF-23; HR-14).
*Why.* Otherwise the card is either a free falsifier or a separate lie target.
*Edge notes.* The card has no module-frame surface, so if the wall shows a stage-3 `whole` frame while the module is `cracked`, the card shows only the reading and there is nothing for it to disagree with. Stress is the one honest-only difference of *form* that may arise (tremor versus the held notch under `reduced_motion`, K-18 resolved by D96); it is honest-only on both and never differs in a lie *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.

#### Group F. Boundaries, content floors and fallbacks

**IW-27. Reduced motion and accessibility substitutes.**
*Rule.* With reduced motion (HR-8): honest settle becomes a **step** (drawn = `displayed_pm`); honest tremor is replaced by a **held stress notch pair** (each `max(NOTCH_PAIR_PX, ceil(NOTCH_MIN_SCREEN_PX / k))` art px, at least 4 screen px at every rung *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), shown while the IW-12 predicate holds **and** `motion_mode` is HONEST, and never on a lying reading (it would be an oracle): the notch pair is removed in the first non-HONEST frame, immediately and not faded (under `reduced_motion` no tremor is drawn, so `tremor_weight_pm` has nothing to blend; PF-8 keeps the immediate clearing of the notch and of the settle triple) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*; the alarm mark holds solid. Glide, wander and lying-tick scaling are the Filter's (PF-39: `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` 0.6, rate floor not below 0.3 deg/s, wander never scaled, lying tick never below `LIE_TICK_MS`) and are not restated. The notch is two Void Steel nicks cut into the world bezel's top edge about 4 px either side of centre, and, on the card, two Hull Grey squares on the Ground plate above the dial *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's placement adopted; R19 said "on the bezel", but HR-2 forbids Hull Grey on a bezel fill, so the card's notch sits on the Ground side of the dial rim)*. No setting removes a leak mode, hides the gleam or the card numeral, or adds an Attention or sanity surface. Instrument labels and the card obey the 21/15 text tier and UI scale `H`; the instrument face is a bitmap font at integer `H` only (advisor ruling R19). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Reduce flashing defaults ON at first launch** (user ruling, D79): the card's honest numeral already rides the shared hold grid (D.3) and adds no flash surface that the default would need to suppress; under the HUD's stricter arbiter for reduce flashing (HS-47) a grid boundary may be skipped and the card shows the then-latest step at the next one, which the lag bound of `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS` already covers. Card tremor is suppressed under `reduced_motion` (IW-12, D96).
*Why.* HR-8: the backbone of the lie (never-rest, continuous tick) survives; tremor is the one signature that needs a static substitute.
*Edge notes.* Accessibility Settings (Alpha) depends on this GDD (IDX:209): its reduced-motion toggle reads the Filter's published scalars (`reduced_motion_glide_pm`, `breath_depth_pm`, `lie_tick_min_ms`) and this rule's substitute *(provisional — Accessibility Settings undesigned)*. The screen-reader text for a card (Alpha) is built from `Perceived.displayed_value` only, never `true_value`; the pinned engine's accessibility live-region maturity is `[UNV]`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Tell survival for a deaf, colour-blind player.** With the sound removed and the hue removed, a lie keeps the never-rest motion mode on the needle, the continuous tick on the card numeral and the gleam as a **luminance** fringe; the claim of at least two tells therefore holds only if the fringe `#B07BE6` keeps at least `GLEAM_LUM_CONTRAST_MIN` 3:1 (the WCAG non-text ratio, `[PLACEHOLDER]`) against the glass it rides in greyscale, measured at S-A1 and tested by AC-IW-120. **Tell-survival rule** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: for every combination of reduced motion (scale 0.6), captions on or off, greyscale or a colour-vision filter, and sound off, at least two of the three tells survive on every lying instrument: the never-resting needle (the wander is never scaled, PF-39), the luminance gleam (above `GLEAM_LUM_CONTRAST_MIN`) and the sound (not counted when sound is off or unheard). The numeral tick is a mode of the motion tell and is not counted as a separate tell. Where reduced motion lengthens a digit hold, D.12 accepts it explicitly (`T_VIS_MAX_RM_S`). Tested by AC-IW-125; the caption tier is recorded in `design/accessibility-requirements.md` once that file exists (OQ-IW-42). Captions for lie sounds (Alpha) are a gate dependency of the accessibility tier and not an Instruments feature. `design/accessibility-requirements.md` does not exist; `/ux-design accessibility` sets the tier (OQ-IW-42).

**IW-28. What Instruments never do (scope guard).**
*Rule.* No schematic, overlay, minimap, ship-status, loop-summary or "lit schematic console" screen, ever; **rejected: lit schematic console** (answers CT:63, CT-1 at CT:223, CT:537 and CT:685 C4; LSG:51 anti-pillar 3). No numerals on a world gauge; no text on an in-world gauge; no closed ring or progress ring (curves are reserved for dial arcs and needles, ART 3.4); no condition word, bar, rating or loot value; no weld-preview number or seam readout (`surge[]` is never printed, LSG:170); no sanity meter, lie counter, "spotted" statistic, stage name or Attention, threat-level, proximity or direction indicator on any instrument (nothing Attention publishes feeds a needle); no instrument shows a horror, a threat level, a proximity or a direction (Pillar 3; HE Interactions downstream); a needle moves only when the ship's loop moves, the tell never moves one, and no instrument displays or sonifies the Attention level (AA UI Requirements; AT-17); no reading of a crewmate or a horror; no Alarm Red word; no violet or flesh pixel in an authored sheet; no pod dash; no new sim state, hook, mutator or block. A lint over the scene asserts that no node outside an instrument or the card renders Graph state at a distance (advisor ruling R16; PF-38; HE:377).
*Why.* Anti-pillars (no combat, no PvP, no authored story, no win state) and P1.

428	| B | `inst_b_dock_p_o2` | DIAL_L (was DIAL_S) | `p_o2` / `b_dock` | `b_spine` -> `b_dock` (**1**) | REMOTE | (d) none | scanner-dependent (REMOTE, no second B `p_o2` gauge) | scanner-dependent (REMOTE, no suit credit) | post-weld leak (not OK): comfort direction; **Beat C fixture B, scanner-dependent** |
429	
430	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1: rewritten against Sanity SN-15 L-2I)* The Filter's `quantity` term (PF-9) and the Graph's published `true_value` kinds (LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27) retired the one-compartment-instrument-per-room fallback, so `inst_cryo_bay_T` is eligible; `inst_engine_bus_load` additionally waits on the Graph's `load_pm` kind (IW-9). **Counts are ranges `[no usable scanner, usable scanner]`, never one number.** *Usable scanner* means the seat carries `tool_scanner` (it is in the start kit, SE-15) and is not carrying a module (SE-11); the scanner credit is the only credit most rows have. With a usable scanner every listed row has a credit: **home 9, A 4, B 5** (18; home 8 if the scanner cannot read `load`, OQ-IW-43). Without one, only rows with a **fixed same-loop gauge in another compartment** stay eligible: **home 3** (`inst_cryo_bay_p_o2`, `inst_engine_room_p_o2`, `inst_scr_main_glyph`), **A 0**, **B 1** (`inst_scr_b_glyph`, credited by the `b_dock` gauge). The three suit-alarm credits (`inst_cryo_bay_T`, `inst_a_life_p_o2`, `inst_b_reactor_T`) are alarm-direction only, hold only while the seat stands in the subject compartment and only while the subject is healthy, so they are listed in the table and **not counted** in the lower end. The ranges are therefore **home [3, 9], A [0, 4], B [1, 5]**, counted by credit (structural eligibility). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The direction a lie can take also depends on the subject's live state (L-D, L-G): `inst_cryo_bay_T` and `inst_b_reactor_T` are hops-0 dials authored in a not-OK band, where Sanity's COOLANT guard (`band_t` of the seat's compartment) invalidates a comfort lie for the only seat that can read them and an alarm lie needs a healthy subject, so they count only once their room is back in OK; the upper ends are for that recovered state (at the authored states, home 8 and B 4). The `suit.warmth` credit on these two rows and the COOLANT guard rest on one assumption, that a compartment `T` dial belongs to the COOLANT loop in `lie_targets.json` (OQ-IW-43 (d)); both hold or neither does. The earlier counts (5, 3 and 4 for home, A and B, with A at the floor) rested on a suit credit for comfort-direction lies that SN-15 L-2I does not grant, and are retired; **derelict A is no longer AT-FLOOR at the upper end (4) and is the weakest site at the lower end (0: every A lie needs the scanner)**. A seat that is hauling salvage then receives no lie on A at all, which is Sanity's accepted consequence of SE-11 (EC-SN-42, EC-SN-62), not a defect here; but "scan everything" must not become dominant for the seat that does carry the scanner, so the lower end is reported and the asks below make it seat-independent. **Which lies the first scanner-less seat sees.** The first lie of a world is ALARM-direction by construction (SN-16), and the alarm credits are the widest (fixed gauge, scanner, or the suit in the seat's own compartment), so the Beat B anchor (`inst_engine_room_p_o2`, fixed partner) fires for every seat; the COMFORT lies (Beat C) need a fixed partner or a usable scanner. **L-2I status of this manifest (floor (i)): satisfied by the scanner for a usable-scanner seat; satisfied without it only where a fixed partner is listed.** Fixed partners exist for the `p_o2` gauges (home: `cryo_bay` plus `engine_room`) and for the scrubber glyphs of home and B (credited by a `p_o2` gauge in another compartment); **not** for A's glyph or A's `p_o2` (the only A `p_o2` gauge is in `a_life`, the glyph's own compartment), for `T` (no second `T` gauge on any site; `suit.warmth` is an alarm-direction credit only), for `P` (no second `P` gauge; the suit credits `T` only), for `inst_engine_bus_load` (no second bus-load reading), the two coolant levels, the home fuel level or the batteries. **P0 asks to Derelict Authoring (replacing the earlier battery-partner ask, which would still leave A scanner-only):** (1) in derelict A, a second `p_o2` dial reading another compartment, for example `inst_a_spine_p_o2` mounted in and reading `a_spine`, which makes `inst_a_life_p_o2`, the new dial and `inst_scr_a_glyph` fixed-credited (A lower end 0 to 3); (2) in derelict B, a second `p_o2` dial reading another compartment, for example `inst_b_spine_p_o2` in `b_spine`, which makes the Beat C fixture `inst_b_dock_p_o2` seat-independent (B lower end 1 to 3). A `T`-loop partner for fixture A is not asked: fixture A stays scanner-dependent (OQ-IW-35). The two asked dials are owed rows and are not added to the 18 above. Counts are indicative; no pod dash (K-10). **No acceptance criterion may assert that the manifest as listed passes floor (i)** (advisor ruling R17); AC-IW-108 and AC-IW-109 run against a test-owned fixture manifest with an explicit `seat_scanner_usable` input.
431	*Why.* Too few eligible surfaces make "scan everything" dominant (SN D.12); a decorative gauge makes a lie a non-event.
432	*Edge notes.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The one-compartment-instrument-per-room fallback is retired: the Filter's `quantity` term in `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` (PF-9) and the Graph's published `true_value` kinds (LS-19 additions) make `inst_cryo_bay_T` eligible beside `inst_cryo_bay_p_o2`. Placement is Derelict Authoring's; the record format and the lints are this GDD's. The glyph rows carry STATE, not REMOTE: a glyph is an 8x8 mark on the module housing, so it is always local to the machine it reports (IW-6, IW-17).
433	
434	**IW-30. Binding validity and the DEAD instrument.**
435	*Rule.* If the bound node is DESTROYED, SALVAGED or ABSENT, or the ref is unresolvable, the instrument shows its **DEAD** frame: a glass hairline crack (1 px Hull Grey diagonal) and the needle snapped to a 4-px stub at a fixed angle (an honest static frame on the sheet); no prompt, no card, no gleam, no tremor, no pip. The DEAD frame is truth-graded (untagged) and cannot lie. A compartment-bound gauge is never DEAD while the compartment exists. A missing Filter datum falls back to the honest path (PF-44). *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's snapped stub over the ux-designer's "needle at the low stop"; a needle at zero would assert "reads empty" instead of "has no reading".)*
436	*Why.* "Dead gauges on a module" are falsifier-map class C (DA); a gauge that vanishes would read as a bug, one that keeps reading would read a destroyed thing.
437	*Edge notes.* The stub is not a lie: no tag, no `lie_surface_id`.
438	
439	**IW-31. Placement record (requested) and subject registration.**
440	*Rule.* Layout and Derelict Authoring are asked for an instrument placement record (registry: `instrument_placement_record`) authored as a `Kit placement` (category `mach` or `prop`) carrying `instrument_id` (a key into `assets/data/instruments/`), `node_ref` or `room_key` plus `quantity`, `mount` WALL_FACE | MACHINE_PANEL, `host_face`, and since the design review `mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node` and an optional `witness_anchor_px` (the screen anchor of the drawn witness, a card keep-out, D.6); Layout's `subject_anchors(section_id)` exposes `anchor_px` so Interaction registers an `INSTRUMENT` subject. The node-to-subject binding that SN-16's lit-entry rule names as its one assumption is authored data here; the sim never queries Instruments at runtime (KRN H10). Derelict Authoring lints `INSTRUMENT_NO_BINDING`, `PANEL_GAUGE_VERB_CONFLICT` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (an INSTRUMENT on a MACHINE_PANEL that also carries an interactable verb target, an ERROR while OQ-IW-39 is open) and the at-least-3-eligible-surfaces floor. *(provisional — routed to Layout and Derelict Authoring)* (advisor ruling R23)
441	*Why.* LY-4's schema has Hardpoint, Anchor, Fixture anchor, Kit placement and Loose slot but no instrument with a Graph binding; without a record the binding lives nowhere.
442	
443	**IW-32. Sound.**
444	*Rule.* Instruments request no sound directly. A lying instrument's sound is the Filter's request (`FA_LIE_SIG_GAUGE` for needle, card (needle and numeral) and glyph; `FA_LIE_SIG_SPRITE` for housing and machine; PF-20; Audio owns assets and mix). An honest instrument's tick, settle and tremor are motion only. Card open and close sounds are UI-bus, Audio-owned, and triggered by a presentation-local `card_opened` / `card_closed` signal Instruments publish (the outbound half of registry `inspect_card_context_signal`; event names `UI_INSTRUMENT_CARD_OPEN` / `_CLOSE` requested, Audio owns the naming) *(provisional — Adaptive Audio reply owed)*. Direction-of-change agreement (AAV-17): the machine frame, the sight-glass and the lamp brightness follow the same Graph value the audio reads; a sagging hum beside a full-speed rotor frame is a contradiction the Presenter must not create unless that frame is the lie.
445	*Why.* The Filter owns lie sounds and Audio owns assets and mix (PF-20); an honest instrument that made its own sound would add a sound channel with no witness value.
446	
447	**IW-33. Pause, restore and hard start.**
448	*Rule.* Pause freezes `present_time` and with it every instrument motion (the world freezes undimmed, ART 7.4); an open card is closed by the pause itself (IW-24, a context change) and is not restored on resume *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)*. On `hard_start` (restore, force_stage) the settle triple, tremor envelope, numeral throttle and cull history are reset: the needle shows `displayed_pm` from the first frame with no settle and no glide ramp, any open card closes, and tremor restarts from its onset ramp if the predicate still holds. A camera cut, zoom step or window resize re-projects every placement and re-chooses the card side by a cut; no settle fires. Instruments persist and replicate nothing (PIPE PR-9; PF-33).
449	*Why.* ART 7.4: the world simply stops, undimmed; a restore must reproduce what the player was shown, so no presentation state may survive it.
450	
451	**IW-34. Fallbacks and cut order.**
452	*Rule.* If the card is cut: `inspect` stays bound and dormant; stage-1 reach loses the card surface (IW-21). If the per-instance gleam transport fails (Filter spike S-1): housing and glyph gleams are cut first, never the needle or the card numeral well. If the terminal-fitting mount is rejected: dials only on MACHINE_PANEL mounts. If the art-director rejects the alarm mark: no mark (sweep and sound only). If the user declines the D96 default (card tremor, suppressed under `reduced_motion`): the held notch on the card in all modes *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The Filter's no-cache wording refresh landed on 2026-10-27 (OQ-IW-1 closed); `prev_honest_pm` and the rest, window and dwell scalars are this GDD's presentation-local scalars (IW-11, C14). Stage-3 machine-frame sets and the stage-2 lamp-housing pair are the cuttable tier (a cut removes SPRITE_SWAP eligibility through `has_both_frames`; routed to Sanity to refresh SN-16's stage-3 `KIND_W` weights if taken); the MVP floor is dial + level sight-glass + card + alarm mark + honest WORN.
453	*Why.* A solo developer's art load is the binding constraint (about 20 sheets at P0); every fallback keeps the P1 and P4 contract and removes only presentation.
454	
455	**IW-35. Flagged, not edited.**
456	*Rule.* Missing index edges (Pipeline PIPE:302, Emitter State EM:339, Failure & Trail soft pair, Sanity lie targets) and the unowned module-presenter row are recorded in Dependencies (K-10, K-11, advisor ruling R26); the stale ART 7.0 / 2.5 pod-dash lines are the art-director's (WM:1187). This GDD edits neither the index, the art bible nor another GDD. The field-check / scanner reading is HUD & Suit Layer's to draw (a hand-tool reading on the hand rail and an honest anchor at MVP, SN-19); Instruments supply only the shared honest-digit mechanism of IW-14 as a reusable component (advisor ruling R15; K-9; refresh owed on BS:1206).
457	*Why.* The index's explicit edges and the neighbours' own rows must not be silently rewritten by a downstream author (producer owns the index; art-director owns the bible).
458	
459	**IW-36. Legibility contract: every figure at every rung.**
460	*Rule.* Every legibility figure in this GDD is stated at **every** zoom rung `k` in [1, `k_auto` + 2] (720p and Steam Deck 1280x800 `k_auto` 2: 1..4; 1080p 3: 1..5; 1440p 4: 1..6; 2160p 6: 1..8) and at HUD scale `H` from `H_default` = max(`k_auto`, 3) (Pipeline registry formula `hud_multiplier`, `H_default = max(k, 3)`; `k` there is the default rung `k_auto`, because the HUD does not change with zoom, PIPE PR-12) to 2 x `H_default` (`HUD_MIN_SCALE` 3), including the Steam Deck case (`H` 3 over `k` 2), the largest field (zoom 1x at 2160p) and the maximum `H` on small displays; the table is D.7. By construction the needle stroke (2 art px) is at least 2 screen px at every rung; the gleam and tremor art-px size is raised only at `k` 1 (D.5, D.9); the world needle's absolute floor is `NEEDLE_SCREEN_MIN_PX` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 24, accessibility tier): DIAL_S at `k` 1 (18 screen px) is below it and is accepted because `k` 1 is a deliberate zoom-out and the card is the precision path; at zoom 1x on 2160p the world dial is a 56-px arc in a 3840-px frame, readable only by pattern and needle, which is the design's weakest point and is carried as a risk, not hidden. Tremor's marginal visibility at `k` 1 on the largest field is acceptable only because instrument tremor is never the only tell: every IW-12 stress source also has a sound or world-witness tell owned by Adaptive Audio or Failure & Trail, so zooming out never removes the warning (IW-12; AC-IW-106).
461	*Why.* Reflexion-log rule: an invariant written against the default must be re-checked whenever a later decision adds reachable states (zoom steps, resolutions).
462	
463	**IW-37. Strings and localisation.**
464	*Rule.* Every string on an instrument or card is a `tr()` StringName key: the label (`name_key`), the unit (`unit_key`) and nothing else; a world gauge carries no text. Labels are never truncated (truncation would make two instruments ambiguous): a label wider than the plate's text width (plate width minus 8 art px) wraps to a second row and the plate grows by 7 art px, and the placement cap is recomputed with the taller plate (D.6). The bitmap instrument face covers the shipped Latin set; scripts it lacks (CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic right-to-left) need a fallback face, and the vector reading face is barred on instruments by ART 7.1 (OQ-IW-14). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The card degrades element by element and is never removed for a locale:** the numeral cells (Latin digits with the slashed zero) and the dial or glass render in every locale, and a `name_key` or `unit_key` containing a glyph the bitmap face lacks falls back, for that one element, to the default-locale (Latin) string and then to the instrument's part-number stencil (`instrument_id`), so the only precision path survives everywhere. The decimal mark follows the locale key and is part of the plate variant. No string says a state, a verdict or a lie (IA-39; PF-38).
465	*Why.* A label that can be mistranslated into a verdict is a P4 oracle; a truncated label makes two instruments ambiguous and breaks the second-opinion check.
466	
467	**IW-38. Diagnostics: a dev-only probe and nothing else.**
468	*Rule.* In development builds only, each instrument exposes a read-only `drawn_value(ref)` (the value it actually drew this frame, answering the Debug Overlay's render-probe ask DO-22, whose `DEFECT_BYPASS` class detects a corruptible node that skipped the Filter) and an `instrument_diag(ref)` record `{instrument_id, ref_key, motion_mode as drawn, settle_active, tremor_active, card_open, state}`. `tremor_active` is true while any tremor offset is being drawn, including a fade with `tremor_weight_pm` > 0; `motion_mode as drawn` may therefore be non-HONEST with `tremor_active` true during the first `TREMOR_BLEND_S` of a lie (not a Debug Overlay DEFECT). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* Both are tagged dev-only and stripped from release builds; neither is a value source for any gameplay or presentation node; neither exposes `true_value` (the Overlay calls that itself, DIAGNOSTIC). Instruments publish a stable integer `ref_key` per instrument (the Filter's, PF-9) and keep four counters for the Overlay and the lints: `diag.instr_pm_clamped` (a `displayed_pm` outside 0..1000 was clamped), `diag.inspect_unresolved` (IW-24), `diag.instr_quantity_collision` and `diag.gleam_over_cap` (IW-16). The Overlay treats an absent probe as `bypass_check: ABSENT`, never clean (DO-22). In development builds only, Instruments registers one diagnostics channel at composition-root time under the Debug Overlay's channel contract (DO-12, `diag_panel_contract`), carrying the counters `diag.instr_pm_clamped`, `diag.inspect_unresolved`, `diag.instr_quantity_collision` and `diag.gleam_over_cap` and the `instrument_diag(ref)` rows. The channel is a dev-only panel registration, not a kernel block, hook, mutator or dirty key, so IW-2's zero-registration rule is unchanged; it is stripped from release builds.
469	*Why.* The Overlay's classifier can otherwise only compare `perceived` with `true_value`; a node that bypasses the Filter is invisible to it.
470	*Edge notes.* An out-of-range `displayed_pm` is clamped to the end stop and counted; it is never an error shown to the player.

**IW-29. The MVP manifest is a content floor plus an indicative list.**
*Rule.* Floors, each a lint over the instrument data and Derelict Authoring's placements: (i) **L-2I per seat and per direction** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1, restated in the words of Sanity SN-15 L-2I)*: a lie on an instrument is eligible for a seat only if the loop keeps at least `SECOND_INSTRUMENT_MIN` (Sanity, value 1) honest second reading drawn from the L-2I list: **a fixed gauge on the same loop in another compartment** (a DIAL or LINEAR instrument reading another compartment's or node's quantity on that loop; a GLYPH is a machine-state mark, not a gauge, and is not credited as a partner, this GDD's reading of "gauge", OQ-IW-43), **or the scanner** (`tool_scanner`, honest in the MVP, SN-19), credited only if the seat carries it and can equip it, which means **not carrying a module** (Suit SE-11: `equip_tool` answers `BUSY` while carrying; Sanity makes no single-instrument-loop lie for a carrying seat), **or, for an ALARM-direction lie only**, `suit.o2` (the `p_o2` loop) or `suit.warmth` (the COOLANT loop's thermal quantity `T` only, Sanity QA-3), each valid only for the seat's current compartment. **For a COMFORT-direction lie the suit is never a credit** (at its activation the seat's compartment band must be OK, L-G, so the suit reading would agree with the lie). `suit.integrity`, `suit.reserve` and `suit.charge` never count. Because the suit reads the seat's own room, a REMOTE row (`hops` >= 1) gets **no suit credit in either direction**. An instrument whose only credit is the scanner is **scanner-dependent, seat-conditional**: it draws no lie for a seat without a usable scanner, so every per-site count is a **range**, not a number (IW-29 counts below); (ii) at least 3 lie-eligible surfaces per site (OQ-SN-11, advisory; AC-SN-134), **counted for a seat that can use the scanner** and reported also for a seat that cannot (carrying a module), so the count is a range `[no usable scanner, usable scanner]` and the gate is on the upper end while the lower end is reported as a finding *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1; which seat Sanity's AC-SN-134 counts for is OQ-IW-43)*; (iii) every instrument has a consequence-channel witness within `WITNESS_HOPS_MAX` 2 (Sanity-owned, L-W; linted by DA-34 against the LS-22 table) that shares no node with it (FT:314, AC-138); (iv) no decorative gauge (SN:262): every record's computed `beyond_witness` set (IW-8) is non-empty (GLYPH and FRAME carry STATE); a local dial on a quantity whose witness is continuous and which is not inertial (a `load` dial in the room of its bus) has an empty set and fails; (v) **no instrument with `hops(mount_room, subject_room)` >= 1 (REMOTE) carries the alarm mark** (stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 1; IW-19): the lint `ALARM_MARK_ON_REMOTE` is `hops >= 1 AND mark_flag`, and it also fails the build when a mark is bound to any subject other than the machine or console panel, tank prop or compartment the housing physically belongs to; (vi) **each derelict has at least one lethal-capable REMOTE instrument with a verified hop count** (lie-eligible, 1 <= `hops` <= `WITNESS_HOPS_MAX`, its subject room carrying a `lethal_fault_modes` fault or a lethal band) as the Beat C fixture (lint `NO_BEAT_C_FIXTURE`, advisory until Sanity rules on cold-band lethality, OQ-IW-35); the proposed fixtures are `inst_b_dock_p_o2` (B) and `inst_a_machine_T` (A) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1)* **Both fixtures are REMOTE and COMFORT-direction, so the suit never credits them and each is scanner-dependent as listed**: the fixture is valid only for a seat with a usable scanner (the lint takes an explicit `seat_scanner_usable` input and passes only when the fixture is comfort-eligible for the seat with it set true; the carrying-seat result is reported, never gated). A fixed same-loop partner would make a fixture seat-independent; that is a P0 ask to Derelict Authoring (below). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1: rewritten against Sanity SN-15 L-2I)* The Filter's `quantity` term (PF-9) and the Graph's published `true_value` kinds (LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27) retired the one-compartment-instrument-per-room fallback, so `inst_cryo_bay_T` is eligible; `inst_engine_bus_load` additionally waits on the Graph's `load_pm` kind (IW-9). **Counts are ranges `[no usable scanner, usable scanner]`, never one number.** *Usable scanner* means the seat carries `tool_scanner` (it is in the start kit, SE-15) and is not carrying a module (SE-11); the scanner credit is the only credit most rows have. With a usable scanner every listed row has a credit: **home 9, A 4, B 5** (18; home 8 if the scanner cannot read `load`, OQ-IW-43). Without one, only rows with a **fixed same-loop gauge in another compartment** stay eligible: **home 3** (`inst_cryo_bay_p_o2`, `inst_engine_room_p_o2`, `inst_scr_main_glyph`), **A 0**, **B 1** (`inst_scr_b_glyph`, credited by the `b_dock` gauge). The three suit-alarm credits (`inst_cryo_bay_T`, `inst_a_life_p_o2`, `inst_b_reactor_T`) are alarm-direction only, hold only while the seat stands in the subject compartment and only while the subject is healthy, so they are listed in the table and **not counted** in the lower end. The ranges are therefore **home [3, 9], A [0, 4], B [1, 5]**, counted by credit (structural eligibility). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The direction a lie can take also depends on the subject's live state (L-D, L-G): `inst_cryo_bay_T` and `inst_b_reactor_T` are hops-0 dials authored in a not-OK band, where Sanity's COOLANT guard (`band_t` of the seat's compartment) invalidates a comfort lie for the only seat that can read them and an alarm lie needs a healthy subject, so they count only once their room is back in OK; the upper ends are for that recovered state (at the authored states, home 8 and B 4). The `suit.warmth` credit on these two rows and the COOLANT guard rest on one assumption, that a compartment `T` dial belongs to the COOLANT loop in `lie_targets.json` (OQ-IW-43 (d)); both hold or neither does. The earlier counts (5, 3 and 4 for home, A and B, with A at the floor) rested on a suit credit for comfort-direction lies that SN-15 L-2I does not grant, and are retired; **derelict A is no longer AT-FLOOR at the upper end (4) and is the weakest site at the lower end (0: every A lie needs the scanner)**. A seat that is hauling salvage then receives no lie on A at all, which is Sanity's accepted consequence of SE-11 (EC-SN-42, EC-SN-62), not a defect here; but "scan everything" must not become dominant for the seat that does carry the scanner, so the lower end is reported and the asks below make it seat-independent. **Which lies the first scanner-less seat sees.** The first lie of a world is ALARM-direction by construction (SN-16), and the alarm credits are the widest (fixed gauge, scanner, or the suit in the seat's own compartment), so the Beat B anchor (`inst_engine_room_p_o2`, fixed partner) fires for every seat; the COMFORT lies (Beat C) need a fixed partner or a usable scanner. **L-2I status of this manifest (floor (i)): satisfied by the scanner for a usable-scanner seat; satisfied without it only where a fixed partner is listed.** Fixed partners exist for the `p_o2` gauges (home: `cryo_bay` plus `engine_room`) and for the scrubber glyphs of home and B (credited by a `p_o2` gauge in another compartment); **not** for A's glyph or A's `p_o2` (the only A `p_o2` gauge is in `a_life`, the glyph's own compartment), for `T` (no second `T` gauge on any site; `suit.warmth` is an alarm-direction credit only), for `P` (no second `P` gauge; the suit credits `T` only), for `inst_engine_bus_load` (no second bus-load reading), the two coolant levels, the home fuel level or the batteries. **P0 asks to Derelict Authoring (replacing the earlier battery-partner ask, which would still leave A scanner-only):** (1) in derelict A, a second `p_o2` dial reading another compartment, for example `inst_a_spine_p_o2` mounted in and reading `a_spine`, which makes `inst_a_life_p_o2`, the new dial and `inst_scr_a_glyph` fixed-credited (A lower end 0 to 3); (2) in derelict B, a second `p_o2` dial reading another compartment, for example `inst_b_spine_p_o2` in `b_spine`, which makes the Beat C fixture `inst_b_dock_p_o2` seat-independent (B lower end 1 to 3). A `T`-loop partner for fixture A is not asked: fixture A stays scanner-dependent (OQ-IW-35). The two asked dials are owed rows and are not added to the 18 above. Counts are indicative; no pod dash (K-10). **No acceptance criterion may assert that the manifest as listed passes floor (i)** (advisor ruling R17); AC-IW-108 and AC-IW-109 run against a test-owned fixture manifest with an explicit `seat_scanner_usable` input.
*Why.* Too few eligible surfaces make "scan everything" dominant (SN D.12); a decorative gauge makes a lie a non-event.
*Edge notes.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The one-compartment-instrument-per-room fallback is retired: the Filter's `quantity` term in `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` (PF-9) and the Graph's published `true_value` kinds (LS-19 additions) make `inst_cryo_bay_T` eligible beside `inst_cryo_bay_p_o2`. Placement is Derelict Authoring's; the record format and the lints are this GDD's. The glyph rows carry STATE, not REMOTE: a glyph is an 8x8 mark on the module housing, so it is always local to the machine it reports (IW-6, IW-17).

**IW-30. Binding validity and the DEAD instrument.**
*Rule.* If the bound node is DESTROYED, SALVAGED or ABSENT, or the ref is unresolvable, the instrument shows its **DEAD** frame: a glass hairline crack (1 px Hull Grey diagonal) and the needle snapped to a 4-px stub at a fixed angle (an honest static frame on the sheet); no prompt, no card, no gleam, no tremor, no pip. The DEAD frame is truth-graded (untagged) and cannot lie. A compartment-bound gauge is never DEAD while the compartment exists. A missing Filter datum falls back to the honest path (PF-44). *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's snapped stub over the ux-designer's "needle at the low stop"; a needle at zero would assert "reads empty" instead of "has no reading".)*
*Why.* "Dead gauges on a module" are falsifier-map class C (DA); a gauge that vanishes would read as a bug, one that keeps reading would read a destroyed thing.
*Edge notes.* The stub is not a lie: no tag, no `lie_surface_id`.

**IW-31. Placement record (requested) and subject registration.**
*Rule.* Layout and Derelict Authoring are asked for an instrument placement record (registry: `instrument_placement_record`) authored as a `Kit placement` (category `mach` or `prop`) carrying `instrument_id` (a key into `assets/data/instruments/`), `node_ref` or `room_key` plus `quantity`, `mount` WALL_FACE | MACHINE_PANEL, `host_face`, and since the design review `mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node` and an optional `witness_anchor_px` (the screen anchor of the drawn witness, a card keep-out, D.6); Layout's `subject_anchors(section_id)` exposes `anchor_px` so Interaction registers an `INSTRUMENT` subject. The node-to-subject binding that SN-16's lit-entry rule names as its one assumption is authored data here; the sim never queries Instruments at runtime (KRN H10). Derelict Authoring lints `INSTRUMENT_NO_BINDING`, `PANEL_GAUGE_VERB_CONFLICT` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (an INSTRUMENT on a MACHINE_PANEL that also carries an interactable verb target, an ERROR while OQ-IW-39 is open) and the at-least-3-eligible-surfaces floor. *(provisional — routed to Layout and Derelict Authoring)* (advisor ruling R23)
*Why.* LY-4's schema has Hardpoint, Anchor, Fixture anchor, Kit placement and Loose slot but no instrument with a Graph binding; without a record the binding lives nowhere.

**IW-32. Sound.**
*Rule.* Instruments request no sound directly. A lying instrument's sound is the Filter's request (`FA_LIE_SIG_GAUGE` for needle, card (needle and numeral) and glyph; `FA_LIE_SIG_SPRITE` for housing and machine; PF-20; Audio owns assets and mix). An honest instrument's tick, settle and tremor are motion only. Card open and close sounds are UI-bus, Audio-owned, and triggered by a presentation-local `card_opened` / `card_closed` signal Instruments publish (the outbound half of registry `inspect_card_context_signal`; event names `UI_INSTRUMENT_CARD_OPEN` / `_CLOSE` requested, Audio owns the naming) *(provisional — Adaptive Audio reply owed)*. Direction-of-change agreement (AAV-17): the machine frame, the sight-glass and the lamp brightness follow the same Graph value the audio reads; a sagging hum beside a full-speed rotor frame is a contradiction the Presenter must not create unless that frame is the lie.
*Why.* The Filter owns lie sounds and Audio owns assets and mix (PF-20); an honest instrument that made its own sound would add a sound channel with no witness value.

**IW-33. Pause, restore and hard start.**
*Rule.* Pause freezes `present_time` and with it every instrument motion (the world freezes undimmed, ART 7.4); an open card is closed by the pause itself (IW-24, a context change) and is not restored on resume *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)*. On `hard_start` (restore, force_stage) the settle triple, tremor envelope, numeral throttle and cull history are reset: the needle shows `displayed_pm` from the first frame with no settle and no glide ramp, any open card closes, and tremor restarts from its onset ramp if the predicate still holds. A camera cut, zoom step or window resize re-projects every placement and re-chooses the card side by a cut; no settle fires. Instruments persist and replicate nothing (PIPE PR-9; PF-33).
*Why.* ART 7.4: the world simply stops, undimmed; a restore must reproduce what the player was shown, so no presentation state may survive it.

**IW-34. Fallbacks and cut order.**
*Rule.* If the card is cut: `inspect` stays bound and dormant; stage-1 reach loses the card surface (IW-21). If the per-instance gleam transport fails (Filter spike S-1): housing and glyph gleams are cut first, never the needle or the card numeral well. If the terminal-fitting mount is rejected: dials only on MACHINE_PANEL mounts. If the art-director rejects the alarm mark: no mark (sweep and sound only). If the user declines the D96 default (card tremor, suppressed under `reduced_motion`): the held notch on the card in all modes *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The Filter's no-cache wording refresh landed on 2026-10-27 (OQ-IW-1 closed); `prev_honest_pm` and the rest, window and dwell scalars are this GDD's presentation-local scalars (IW-11, C14). Stage-3 machine-frame sets and the stage-2 lamp-housing pair are the cuttable tier (a cut removes SPRITE_SWAP eligibility through `has_both_frames`; routed to Sanity to refresh SN-16's stage-3 `KIND_W` weights if taken); the MVP floor is dial + level sight-glass + card + alarm mark + honest WORN.
*Why.* A solo developer's art load is the binding constraint (about 20 sheets at P0); every fallback keeps the P1 and P4 contract and removes only presentation.

**IW-35. Flagged, not edited.**
*Rule.* Missing index edges (Pipeline PIPE:302, Emitter State EM:339, Failure & Trail soft pair, Sanity lie targets) and the unowned module-presenter row are recorded in Dependencies (K-10, K-11, advisor ruling R26); the stale ART 7.0 / 2.5 pod-dash lines are the art-director's (WM:1187). This GDD edits neither the index, the art bible nor another GDD. The field-check / scanner reading is HUD & Suit Layer's to draw (a hand-tool reading on the hand rail and an honest anchor at MVP, SN-19); Instruments supply only the shared honest-digit mechanism of IW-14 as a reusable component (advisor ruling R15; K-9; refresh owed on BS:1206).
*Why.* The index's explicit edges and the neighbours' own rows must not be silently rewritten by a downstream author (producer owns the index; art-director owns the bible).

**IW-36. Legibility contract: every figure at every rung.**
*Rule.* Every legibility figure in this GDD is stated at **every** zoom rung `k` in [1, `k_auto` + 2] (720p and Steam Deck 1280x800 `k_auto` 2: 1..4; 1080p 3: 1..5; 1440p 4: 1..6; 2160p 6: 1..8) and at HUD scale `H` from `H_default` = max(`k_auto`, 3) (Pipeline registry formula `hud_multiplier`, `H_default = max(k, 3)`; `k` there is the default rung `k_auto`, because the HUD does not change with zoom, PIPE PR-12) to 2 x `H_default` (`HUD_MIN_SCALE` 3), including the Steam Deck case (`H` 3 over `k` 2), the largest field (zoom 1x at 2160p) and the maximum `H` on small displays; the table is D.7. By construction the needle stroke (2 art px) is at least 2 screen px at every rung; the gleam and tremor art-px size is raised only at `k` 1 (D.5, D.9); the world needle's absolute floor is `NEEDLE_SCREEN_MIN_PX` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 24, accessibility tier): DIAL_S at `k` 1 (18 screen px) is below it and is accepted because `k` 1 is a deliberate zoom-out and the card is the precision path; at zoom 1x on 2160p the world dial is a 56-px arc in a 3840-px frame, readable only by pattern and needle, which is the design's weakest point and is carried as a risk, not hidden. Tremor's marginal visibility at `k` 1 on the largest field is acceptable only because instrument tremor is never the only tell: every IW-12 stress source also has a sound or world-witness tell owned by Adaptive Audio or Failure & Trail, so zooming out never removes the warning (IW-12; AC-IW-106).
*Why.* Reflexion-log rule: an invariant written against the default must be re-checked whenever a later decision adds reachable states (zoom steps, resolutions).

**IW-37. Strings and localisation.**
*Rule.* Every string on an instrument or card is a `tr()` StringName key: the label (`name_key`), the unit (`unit_key`) and nothing else; a world gauge carries no text. Labels are never truncated (truncation would make two instruments ambiguous): a label wider than the plate's text width (plate width minus 8 art px) wraps to a second row and the plate grows by 7 art px, and the placement cap is recomputed with the taller plate (D.6). The bitmap instrument face covers the shipped Latin set; scripts it lacks (CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic right-to-left) need a fallback face, and the vector reading face is barred on instruments by ART 7.1 (OQ-IW-14). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The card degrades element by element and is never removed for a locale:** the numeral cells (Latin digits with the slashed zero) and the dial or glass render in every locale, and a `name_key` or `unit_key` containing a glyph the bitmap face lacks falls back, for that one element, to the default-locale (Latin) string and then to the instrument's part-number stencil (`instrument_id`), so the only precision path survives everywhere. The decimal mark follows the locale key and is part of the plate variant. No string says a state, a verdict or a lie (IA-39; PF-38).
*Why.* A label that can be mistranslated into a verdict is a P4 oracle; a truncated label makes two instruments ambiguous and breaks the second-opinion check.

**IW-38. Diagnostics: a dev-only probe and nothing else.**
*Rule.* In development builds only, each instrument exposes a read-only `drawn_value(ref)` (the value it actually drew this frame, answering the Debug Overlay's render-probe ask DO-22, whose `DEFECT_BYPASS` class detects a corruptible node that skipped the Filter) and an `instrument_diag(ref)` record `{instrument_id, ref_key, motion_mode as drawn, settle_active, tremor_active, card_open, state}`. `tremor_active` is true while any tremor offset is being drawn, including a fade with `tremor_weight_pm` > 0; `motion_mode as drawn` may therefore be non-HONEST with `tremor_active` true during the first `TREMOR_BLEND_S` of a lie (not a Debug Overlay DEFECT). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* Both are tagged dev-only and stripped from release builds; neither is a value source for any gameplay or presentation node; neither exposes `true_value` (the Overlay calls that itself, DIAGNOSTIC). Instruments publish a stable integer `ref_key` per instrument (the Filter's, PF-9) and keep four counters for the Overlay and the lints: `diag.instr_pm_clamped` (a `displayed_pm` outside 0..1000 was clamped), `diag.inspect_unresolved` (IW-24), `diag.instr_quantity_collision` and `diag.gleam_over_cap` (IW-16). The Overlay treats an absent probe as `bypass_check: ABSENT`, never clean (DO-22). In development builds only, Instruments registers one diagnostics channel at composition-root time under the Debug Overlay's channel contract (DO-12, `diag_panel_contract`), carrying the counters `diag.instr_pm_clamped`, `diag.inspect_unresolved`, `diag.instr_quantity_collision` and `diag.gleam_over_cap` and the `instrument_diag(ref)` rows. The channel is a dev-only panel registration, not a kernel block, hook, mutator or dirty key, so IW-2's zero-registration rule is unchanged; it is stripped from release builds.
*Why.* The Overlay's classifier can otherwise only compare `perceived` with `true_value`; a node that bypasses the Filter is invisible to it.
*Edge notes.* An out-of-range `displayed_pm` is clamped to the end stop and counted; it is never an error shown to the player.

- Life-Support Graph `read_view` (LS-19): `compartment(cid)`, `node(id)`/`edge(id)` (`state`, `sev`, `served_pm`, `hp`), `loop_component`, `failures(filter)` (incl. `alarm_eligible`, hazard modes, `SEAL_STRAIN`), `nodes_in(cid)`, `neighbors(cid)`, `section_of(id)`, `stress_active(section_id)` (optional, off); LS-7 band names at build time; LS-11/LS-13/LS-14 descriptors; LS-20 dirty-key quanta; requested `load_pm` kind

- Interaction System: `focus_view`, `INSTRUMENT` subjects via `sync_section`, `verb_inspect` (IA-38), prompt debounce `PROMPT_SHOW_DEBOUNCE_TICKS` 13 (IA-37, IA-39, AC-IA-112)
- Player Controller & Input: Adapter's `{context, inspect_ref}` signal, `inspect_card` context, `inspect`/`cancel`/B, `set_aim`, `MOVE_DEADZONE` (PC-2, PC-6, PC-16)
- Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera: `world_to_hud(pos)` (C11), `H`, `k`, `k_auto`, `tick_alpha`, `present_time` (PR-9), PR-8 rules, `HUD_MIN_SCALE`, layers 0 and 2
- HUD & Suit Layer: layer-2 `CanvasLayer`, `ui_theme_main`, bezel nine-slice, keycap, tabular-numeral label, gleam-on-glass helper (HS-48), `HONEST_TICK_MS` grid, flash arbiter (HS-14, HS-47)
- 2D Lighting & Occlusion: HullSurface, emissive layer mask bit 2, LO-13 five-material budget, `PIP_EMIT_MAX`
- Sanity & Hallucination Rules: `lie_targets.json`, SN-15 L-2I, SN-16 reach, SN-23 `subject_ref` surface enum, AC-SN-152
- Item & Module Database: `sprite_family`, state tokens (`running`, `stopped`, `whole`, `cracked`, lamp pair)
- Ship Section & Layout / Derelict Authoring: `subject_anchors(section_id)`, authored placements, DA-34 lints
- Command & Simulation Layer: `PRESENTATION` subscriber class, dirty-mark notifications, restore event
- Adaptive Audio & Tells (UI bus assets), Debug Overlay (DO-12 `diag_panel_contract`, DO-22), Accessibility Settings (provisional: reduced-motion scalars, UI scale), Failure & Trail (witness existence, lint only), Suit & Equipment / Web Map (O2 tank and fuel tank sight-glasses)

## Engine risk

- CanvasItem / Sprite2D with NEAREST filtering and integer base-px placement, no antialiased draw lines (the GDD cites "4.7 `CanvasItem` line drawing has no antialiasing feather", `[REF]` breaking-changes.md): HIGH (4.7 behaviour is relied on)
- Per-instance CanvasItem shader parameters (instance uniforms) for the gleam, marked `[UNV]` for 4.7.2: HIGH; fallback is a child edge sprite with `modulate.a`
- Sprite2D rotation under NEAREST at `k` 1..8 (spike S-A3, AC-IW-54): MEDIUM (unverified; baseline avoids runtime rotation by pre-rendered frames)
- ShaderMaterial / CanvasItem material budget (LO-13 five materials) and draw-call batching of up to 20 instruments: MEDIUM
- Light2D / lit renderer with HullSurface material and the emissive layer (mask bit 2): LOW (core Godot 2D lighting; per-project mask scheme is owned by Lighting)
- Control focus: `mouse_filter` IGNORE and `focus_mode` NONE, "4.6 dual focus" (UI-4, AC-IW-53): HIGH (4.6 dual-focus behaviour)
- CanvasLayer (layer 2) with a single `Theme`, bezel nine-slice (`StyleBoxTexture`), integer-scale bitmap font at integer `H`: LOW; tabular numerals / slashed-zero shaping and integer snapping of a vector font are `[UNV]` for the pinned build: MEDIUM
- `tr()` with StringName keys and locale fallbacks; accessibility live-region / screen-reader text (AccessKit, 4.5): HIGH (maturity `[UNV]`, Alpha scope only)
- `Input` / action contexts and gamepad stick dead-zone handling (inspect_card context, `CARD_PAD_DEADZONE_MARGIN`): LOW
- AudioServer / UI bus for card open/close/unlatch cues (Audio-owned): LOW
- Frame timing: `_process` render-callback reads with `tick_alpha` interpolation and `present_time` freezing on pause: LOW
- Reduced-motion / reduce-flashing rendering substitutes (no special engine feature): LOW
